s: David Berman said the song was ‘about making music, a statement of intent’.
David Berman tried to make the album Purple Mountains with Dan Auerbach, Dan Bejar, Stephen Malkmus and Jeff Tweedy before recording it in 2018 with members of Woods.
Titus Andronicus played it at DCBday, a show at New York's Bowery Ballroom marking what would have been David Berman's 58th birthday.
David Berman made the album Purple Mountains partly to pay down more than $100,000 of credit card debt and loans.
Grizzly Bear's Daniel Rossen, the album's only featured guest, got involved after Hannah Frances sent him an Instagram DM, and helped produce and arrange the song.
Hannah Frances described it as ‘a haywire and whimsical exploration of familial rupture’.
Vanessa Castro directed its spooky video, in which Hannah Frances haunts a farmhouse.
Hannah Frances recorded its album, Nested in Tangles, in Arlington, Vermont, with her longtime collaborator Kevin Copeland, and friends added horn, wind and string arrangements.
Hannah Frances wrote Nested in Tangles throughout 2023 and 2024, inspired by her experiments with open guitar tunings.
Its lyrics, like those of ‘The Golden One’, were lifted directly from Whitmer Thomas's early hardships, and the two songs drew particular critical attention.
Whitmer Thomas filmed his special The Golden One in 2019 at the Flora-Bama Lounge, where his mother and aunt's new wave duo Syn Twister were the house band.
Whitmer Thomas wrote and performed all nine original songs in The Golden One, which closes with a cover of ‘He's Hot’ by his mother's band, Syn Twister.
Whitmer Thomas's comedy special The Golden One was executive-produced by Bo Burnham, whom Thomas had opened for on the 2016 Make Happy tour.
Alex Cameron released it as a stand-alone single on 13 October 2025, producing it with Mark Perkins, with extra instrumentation from Maxim Ludwig.
Alex Cameron, Mark Perkins and Maxim Ludwig, the trio behind it, went on to make Cameron's fifth album, Late to Set, released on 24 July 2026.
Mark Perkins and Maxim Ludwig, who worked on it, are now Alex Cameron's backing band; saxophonist Roy Molloy, his ‘business partner’, played with him from 2012 to 2024.
Fiona Apple produced The Idler Wheel... with her touring drummer Charley Drayton instead of Jon Brion, and Epic only learned of it when she presented it in early 2012.
Asked by BlackBook when the sessions for The Idler Wheel... began, Fiona Apple said: ‘It must have started in 2008. Or 2009. I don't know!’
Fiona Apple held back The Idler Wheel..., planned for 2011, until Epic found a new president, as she ‘didn't want her work to be mishandled amid corporate disarray’.
The Idler Wheel... gave Fiona Apple her highest US debut, at number 3, and in 2020 Rolling Stone ranked it 213th of the 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.
audiobooks described it as the soundtrack to a party on the verge of chaos in a hip LA hotel, one you sneak into disguised as a cleaner.
audiobooks lit, filmed and directed its video themselves, using one complete unedited take of dancer and choreographer Catarina Carvalho, formerly of Studio Wayne McGregor.
God Is in the TV heard in it the post-funk playfulness of Talking Heads welded to vocal explosions recalling Björk's most frenetic moments.
Sam Swinson of Ohtis got the idea on an oceanfront balcony in Cambria; most of the rest was written and recorded late at night in an Amsterdam hotel room.
Stef Chura joined after someone on Instagram kept asking her to make a song with Ohtis; she ran a poll as a joke, ‘which led to the inevitable’.
A press release called it a character study of ‘the Selfish Antisocial Male’, told mostly through his long put-upon girlfriend, played by Stef Chura.
It was mixed by Collin Dupuis, who has worked with Lana Del Rey, Angel Olsen and St. Vincent.
Rubblebucket wrote it last of all the songs on Survival Sounds, just as they were starting to record the album.
Ben Lovett of Mumford & Sons, founder of Rubblebucket's label Communion, set Alex Toth a song a day for a month; over half of Survival Sounds came from them.
Rubblebucket played it at Boston's Paradise Rock Club on 9 November 2014, the last show of their autumn tour, complete with confetti cannons, glitter balloons and crowd-surfing.
It's on Survival Sounds, recorded at Mission Sound Studio in Brooklyn and produced and mixed by John Congleton, whose credits include St. Vincent and David Byrne.
Paul Simon visited Brazil five times in 1988 and 1989, encouraged by Eddie Palmieri's remark that ‘the journey of the drum goes with the slave trade’.
Paul Simon built many tracks on The Rhythm of the Saints around polyrhythmic percussion patterns, which he said influenced some of the melodies and lyrics added later.
Less than three days before The Rhythm of the Saints was due to ship to shops, Paul Simon postponed it, unhappy with the mixes and track order.
It's on The Rhythm of the Saints, which was inspired by Brazilian musical traditions, much as Paul Simon's previous album, Graceland, drew on South African music.
Theo Katzman recorded Be the Wheel, his fourth album, live to tape at Cinnamon Ranch, his own studio in Michigan.
Theo Katzman called Be the Wheel, the album it names, ‘the most personal and most collaborative album I've made’.
Joe Dart played bass on Be the Wheel, with Jordan Rose on drums and Dave Mackay on keyboards; Philip Weinrobe recorded and mixed it.

Bob Segarini recorded its album, Gotta Have Pop!, at Puck's Farm.
Blondie later had a hit with its own ‘Sunday Girl’, a song with different words and, according to lawyers, unfortunately also a different tune.
We Are Cult's Huw Thomas called it an infectious sunshine pop single from 1973, and asked why buyers of The First Class's ‘Beach Baby’ ignored it.
Bill Morrison and Keith Baker wrote this five-part harmony song, the A-side of Dunno's second record; Dick Pentland wrote and performed its B-side, ‘Magic Beat’.
Its co-writer Bill Morrison had formed Chips, which became one of Ireland's most popular touring bands and featured a young Linda Martin, later a Eurovision winner.
It resurfaced in 2020 on Bubblerock Is Here To Stay!, a box set from Cherry Red's Grapefruit imprint collecting early-1970s pop that once competed for pocket money.
Explaining a line in it on NPR's Fresh Air, Stew said that when a relationship ends he feels he needs “24-hour surveillance”.
Heidi Rodewald said the early Making It songs were exactly how she felt; when Stew wanted her to write her side, she replied: “this is how we both feel, actually”.
Stew had planned to make Making It without Heidi Rodewald but coaxed her into writing about their relationship. “It was like a demon I had to exorcise,” he told NPR.
Stew and his songwriting partner Heidi Rodewald broke up during Passing Strange's first run in Berkeley, California.
It was the first song Phyliss McKoy Joubert ever wrote, and was sung by a group of children she christened the Celestial Choir.
Releases since 2003 have credited a ‘Larry Levan remix’ of it, but no Larry Levan remix exists.
It was recorded in a church in Crown Heights, Brooklyn, by the congregation, for the congregation.
The DJ Tony Humphries heard it while working at Birdel’s Records in Bed-Stuy, and began playing it at Zanzibar in New Jersey.
Its video was filmed in Tom A. Smith's living room with a 1994 camcorder.
Tom A. Smith wrote and finished it in a few hours; he says everything just flowed.
Tom A. Smith has linked it to hearing Dave Stewart describe ‘Sweet Dreams’ as essentially a blues song played on synths.
Barry Hyde of The Futureheads produced it, offering his studio and his time because he absolutely loved the song.
Goody Music Production released a 2025 remaster on the compilation Italo Electro Disco EP 05, crediting Mauro Falzoni and Charles Rolando as its writers.
It was recorded at Fonoprint Studios in Bologna; its credits list a Synclavier, an Emulator, an OB-X, a Jupiter-8 and MC-8 programming.
The label Full Time released it on 3 March 1983, on Peter Richard's album Frozen Red.
It’s on Dream House, made entirely of songs JW Francis wrote for fans who sent him the name of their Valentine and the reason they loved them.
JW Francis got over 300 requests from fans to write songs for their loved ones in three years; some Dream House songs were reworked to speak more to his life.
At The Barrier heard it as ‘Status Quo meets OMD, with Lou Reed on vocals’, and possibly the strongest track on Dream House.
Spin picked it out as Dream House’s song of ‘dizzy romance’, beside tracks about ‘glorious hedonism’ and ‘sweet mundanity’.
Darby Slick wrote it about his own parents, Jeannie Piersol said in the liner notes of her anthology The Nest.
Minnie Riperton, then a member of Rotary Connection, sang the backing vocals.
Released in 1969 on Chess Records' psychedelic offshoot Cadet Concept, it has lately become a chill-out favourite, ‘lionized by DJs, reprised by indie rockers’.
It is the title track of The Nest, an anthology gathering the handful of tracks Jeannie Piersol recorded in her all-too-brief career.
Del Shannon discovered Smith in a Los Angeles nightclub and arranged ‘Baby It’s You’ for the group, which got them signed to ABC-Dunhill Records.
It sold over a million copies between July and October 1969, out-charting the popular versions by the Beatles and the Shirelles.
Quentin Tarantino used it in his 2007 film Death Proof.
Burt Bacharach, Luther Dixon (credited as Barney Williams) and Mack David wrote it, and the Shirelles first took it to No. 8 in 1961.
Dr. Dog released it on Shame, Shame in 2010; it later exploded on TikTok and became the band’s first Platinum record.
Paste’s Justin Jacobs called it the best track on Dr. Dog’s Shame, Shame, its Mellotron, backing harmonies and quick guitar licks ‘all playing like a Pet Sounds B-side’.
On record a ‘shadowy soul number’, Dr. Dog’s song turned into ‘thunderous arena-rock’ live in 2010 when new drummer Eric Slick took hold of it.
Du Blonde has said ‘Take One For The Team’ sounds joyful but is really about a stalker, delivered with her usual dark sense of humour.
At Swan Dive during South by Southwest, Victor Jones, shirt plastered to his body with sweat, performed lines from his six-minute track ‘Shoulder Song’, the Austin Chronicle reported.

1ll45mCZIveI9KHNZx2DdS.name: Purple Mountains
f: Purple Mountains was the indie rock project of musician and poet David Berman, debuting in May 2019, over a decade after his band Silver Jews broke up.
He said a 6.7/10 Pitchfork review of Silver Jews' last album, Lookout Mountain, Lookout Sea, ‘really burned me for a long time’, so he walked away.
The name Purple Mountains comes from a common mishearing of a line in ‘America the Beautiful’; it was also the name of his blog.
Starting over, he lived in a spare room at the office of his long-time record label, the Chicago indie Drag City.
He commissioned a remix of ‘All My Happiness Is Gone’ from the Avalanches, but a licensing issue stopped it being released.

6Xep0FcobRPss2EjGf3ewz.name: Hannah Frances
f: She has been taking dance, piano, trumpet and voice lessons since the age of five.
Her album Keeper of the Shepherd is a meditation on love and loss, born of what its press materials called ‘grief spurred by the death of her father’.
Born in 1997, she won Pitchfork's Best New Music for her 2024 album Keeper of the Shepherd.
She is inspired by the guitar work and confessional songwriting of artists like Joni Mitchell and Nick Drake.
She lives in the woods of Vermont, with roots in Chicago.

2N7DBqf05DIw5tqKLRAUq4.name: Daniel Rossen
f: He did about two rehearsals with Grizzly Bear and worked one of his songs into the set; a week later he was on a two-month tour.
In 2007 he recorded a cover of JoJo's ‘Too Little Too Late’ for his Grizzly Bear bandmate Ed Droste's 29th birthday.
He and Grizzly Bear bandmate Christopher Bear composed the music for the 2023 Academy Award-nominated film Past Lives.
His 2012 solo EP Silent Hour/Golden Mile was made up of songs he had written for Grizzly Bear's next album that went unused.
He is the grandchild of the filmmaker Robert Rossen.

6conzu32k403L1Zr3xWTr1.name: Whitmer Thomas
f: His impression of Blink-182's Tom DeLonge caught Mark Hoppus's attention; the two play in a comedy cover band, Snake Plissken and The I Thought You Were Deads.
In 2014 he and his friend Clay Tatum became executive producers of the FXX cartoon Stone Quackers, voicing its two duck heroes, based on their teenage selves.
In his 2020 ‘Big Baby’ videos an Instagram filter de-ages his face as he sings nonsense; they passed one million views.
For over four years his comedy troupe Power Violence played every Sunday night on Santa Monica Boulevard, using elaborate props and stunts.
In Terminal Crew of Dudes, released by HBO in August 2026, he performs with a backing band of his brother, Johnny, and friends he grew up skateboarding with.

6kGMx9MqwnbKR2EYvZvvrG.name: Alex Cameron
f: Indie duo Foxygen spotted him playing David Lynch's Paris club Silencio; Foxygen's Jonathan Rado went on to produce his album Forced Witness.
In 2018 he and saxophonist Roy Molloy held a 24-hour online telethon to ‘save the music industry and pad our pantry out’, and sold 1,000 records.
He began his solo career playing a failed entertainer, saying he writes about ‘the table-for-one guy’ because ‘failure has been underexplored in music’.
He co-wrote five songs on the Killers' Wonderful Wonderful, and their frontman Brandon Flowers appears on ‘Politics of Love’, which closes Cameron's album Forced Witness.
When Secretly Canadian signed him in 2016, his statement billed him as ‘Entertainer. Showman. Shaman.’, until then playing to ‘a dedicated audience of no one’.

3g2kUQ6tHLLbmkV7T4GPtL.name: Fiona Apple
f: The full title of her 1999 album When the Pawn... is a poem she wrote; its length put it in the Guinness Book of Records for 2001.
She shelved the first version of Extraordinary Machine, reportedly unhappy with the production; fans, wrongly believing Epic Records was withholding it, protested against the label.
She sang with Johnny Cash on his cover of Simon & Garfunkel's ‘Bridge over Troubled Water’, which earned a Grammy nomination.
In 1994 she gave a demo tape to a friend who babysat for publicist Kathryn Schenker, who passed it to Sony Music executive Andy Slater, who signed her.
Her debut album, Tidal, was made up of songs written in her teens, and its single ‘Criminal’ won the Grammy for Best Female Rock Performance.

1YvLqwm8xl6ENUT3KK6XMj.name: audiobooks
f: audiobooks paired David Wrench, one of the most in-demand mixers and producers in modern music, with Evangeline Ling, then a 21-year-old art student from Wimbledon.
Evangeline Ling and David Wrench met at a mutual friend's party a week after Wrench moved to London; they started making music together the next day.
The duo grew from odd stories Evangeline Ling wrote as text messages; David Wrench told her: ‘Come into the studio and let's put them to music.’
They work fast: the duo say they've never spent more than an hour on a track.

3u39r3hiQU2sq7VrV38L6x.name: Ohtis
f: From Normal, Illinois, they formed in high school nearly 20 years before releasing ‘Schatze’.
They released their debut album, Curve of Earth, in 2019; NME called it ‘a record 15 years in the making’.
The band's Adam Pressley is an old friend of Stef Chura's, and was living down the street from her in Detroit when their collaboration was first discussed.

1mZ4u1cMEPjsu6uEa6OxCq.name: Stef Chura
f: After a close friend died, she resolved to make an album: ‘what do I have to do before I die? I have to at least make one record.’
She recorded David Berman's ‘How to Rent a Room’ after his death, having already played it live; she called it a song she ‘could never let go of’.
Will Toledo of Car Seat Headrest produced her 2018 Record Store Day 7-inch: two songs cut from her debut album, Messes.
After moving to Detroit in 2012, she home-recorded and self-released her songs while playing bass in friends' bands.

6xriZDSK3wPXhOoZXr9fzF.name: Rubblebucket
f: At Glastonbury in 2014 they played as Arcade Fire's ‘The Reflektors’, wearing massive papier-mâché heads as a fake-out to fans.
Their first song grew out of music Alex Toth and Annakalmia Traver improvised at a party with percussionist Craig Myers, whom they met in June 2007.
Their 2024 album Year of the Banana is based on a book of poetry Annakalmia Traver wrote in 2015.
Their cover of the Beatles' ‘Michelle’ made Paste magazine's list of the 50 Greatest Beatles Covers of All Time.
They are among the bands, with Red Hot Chili Peppers, Arcade Fire and TV on the Radio, to have covered Fugazi's ‘Waiting Room’.

2CvCyf1gEVhI0mX6aFXmVI.name: Paul Simon
f: While writing ‘Mrs. Robinson’, he toyed with calling it ‘Mrs. Roosevelt’; director Mike Nichols replied: ‘Don't be ridiculous! We're making a movie here!’
At 12 or 13 he wrote his first song, ‘The Girl for Me’; the paper his father wrote it out on is now in the Library of Congress.
He was ‘horrified’ when producer Tom Wilson overdubbed electric guitar, bass and drums onto ‘The Sound of Silence’ without telling him; it went to number 1.
In 1957 he and Art Garfunkel recorded ‘Hey, Schoolgirl’ as Tom & Jerry, a name their label gave them; it reached number 49 on the Billboard charts.
He has won 16 Grammy Awards, three of them for Album of the Year, and has twice been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

2a4lU7F8toqKpb5v6Ftqya.name: Theo Katzman
f: His father, Lee Katzman, played jazz trumpet in the big bands of Stan Kenton, Benny Goodman, Buddy Rich and Gene Krupa.
He is a founding member of Vulfpeck, formed in 2011 as a four-piece instrumental group with him on guitar, drums and vocals.
His maternal grandparents, flautist Albert Tipton and pianist Mary Norris, played with the Detroit, St. Louis and Philadelphia orchestras.
He previewed his 2020 album Modern Johnny Sings with two EPs: Modern Johnny Tackles the Issues and Modern Johnny Wallows in Introspection and Gently Goes Mad.
In 2013 he was musical director and opening act on Darren Criss's national tour, Listen Up.

3yxZJMBn5A2OMEGO7Tvg72.name: Tele Novella
f: The band's Natalie Ribbons moved to Austin because of a bar: a friend took her to Rio Rita Lounge’s ‘Bring Your Own Records Night’, and that was it.
Their songs didn’t sound medieval or western until they were recorded, says Natalie Ribbons; that theme then became the band’s starting point.
They ended up in the small town of Lockhart, Texas; their ‘Vampire Cowgirl’ video was partly shot at a local restaurant, Little Trouble.
After Agent Ribbons split, Natalie Ribbons formed the band with bassist Jason Chronis and drummer Matt Simon; Sarah La Puerta later joined on keyboards and vocals.

7x83XhcMbOTl1UdYsPTuZM.name: Tom Waits
f: He decided to go into show business after watching Lightnin’ Hopkins slam a door marked ‘KEEP OUT. This room is for entertainers ONLY.’
Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2011, he said people call him hitless and difficult to work with, ‘like it’s a bad thing!’
Opening for Frank Zappa’s Mothers of Invention, he faced hostile crowds who jeered at him and pelted him with fruit.
He has said his gravelly singing voice was inspired by the raspy timbre of an uncle’s voice.
Working at Napoleone’s pizza restaurant in National City, California, he wrote down phrases and snippets of dialogue he overheard from customers.

0YMVzWF9HWGbV4DZHfCyKo.name: Divorce
f: They decided to form while sitting on a hill in Nottingham, and each member agreed to take up a different instrument from the one they already played.
They found Hand In Hive, the label for their debut EP, the old-fashioned way: by sending demos to any label address they could find.
Their first ever gig, opening for TV Priest at the Shacklewell Arms in London, was played in the round, with the band in the middle of the room.
They describe themselves as ‘Wilco meets ABBA’, and named Perfume Genius, Belle and Sebastian and Queen as inspirations for their debut album, Drive to Goldenhammer.
After Adam Peter-Smith and Kasper Sandstrøm left in May 2026, Tiger Cohen-Towell and Felix Mackenzie-Barrow carried on the band as a duo.

6fLrPFLWLSCrp7gcTZXcKb.name: Twin Shadow
f: He appears in Grand Theft Auto V as a fictional version of himself, DJ of Radio Mirror Park, which plays ‘Old Love / New Love’, made for the game.
The New York Times said he was ‘giving Kanye West a run for his money as the music world’s leading fashion dilettante’.
He composed the runway music for the fashion label Public School at New York Fashion Week, and has modelled for the brand on and off the runway.
He published a novel, The Night of the Silver Sun, in 2012; it inspired the video saga for ‘Five Seconds’ and ‘Patient’.
His debut album, Forget (2010), was produced by Chris Taylor of Grizzly Bear.

4Ui2kfOqGujY81UcPrb5KE.name: HAIM
f: For their first gig, Este, Danielle and Alana Haim played a Jewish deli in Hollywood and were paid in matzah ball soup.
A high school drama teacher once told Este Haim she was never going to be on Saturday Night Live; the band later played the show as musical guests.
Their mother, Donna Haim, won a contest on The Gong Show in the 1970s singing a Bonnie Raitt song; their father, Moti Haim, had been a professional footballer in Israel.
As children, they played in their parents’ covers band, Rockinhaim, doing free gigs at churches, schools and hospitals.
Danielle Haim toured as a guitarist with Jenny Lewis and then Julian Casablancas before the trio became a full-time band in 2012.

1GWV70Reko15eV2nHCm0bM.name: The Blue Nile
f: The band’s Paul Joseph ‘PJ’ Moore bought a zinc tray from a waiter; they sampled it, and he made a £3 pad to trigger the sound.
They traded a guitar for an effects pedal and borrowed an old drum machine that only played Latin American rhythms; Paul Buchanan admits ‘we were terrible’.
Contrary to legend, hi-fi maker Linn didn’t commission them to show off its equipment, and when Linn offered a record deal, the band took nine months to reply.
The Blue Nile were first called McIntyre, after the University of Glasgow’s administrative offices; they later took their name from Alan Moorehead’s 1962 book.
In September 1990, they became the first non-classical band to play the newly opened Glasgow Royal Concert Hall.

1ybAN3utgdoUL1MUCtH4QM.name: Tennis
f: The band's Alaina Moore and Patrick Riley met in a philosophy class at the University of Colorado Denver; Moore had meant to go to law school.
Alaina Moore and Patrick Riley started the band after an eight-month sailing expedition along the Eastern Atlantic Seaboard; their first album documents the voyage.
In 2021 they made ‘Borrowed Time’ with the cartoon Rick and Morty; it aired in ‘Forgetting Sarick Mortshall’, episode 9 of season 5.
Their second album, Young & Old (2012), was produced by Patrick Carney of the Black Keys.
They were picked to play ‘The Music of David Lynch’, an event hosted by the David Lynch Foundation at the Ace Hotel in Los Angeles.

3IXBujNySf3RBaGjDI8dqm.name: Jane Wiedlin
f: She co-founded the Go-Go’s with Belinda Carlisle in 1978 and designed and sold punk clothes as ‘Jane Drano’ at Granny Takes a Trip on Sunset Boulevard.
She and her Go-Go’s bandmate Charlotte Caffey co-wrote Keith Urban’s first number one, ‘But for the Grace of God’.
She is an ordained minister of the Universal Life Church and, as ‘Reverend Sister Go-Go’, mainly officiates at weddings.
She played the singing telegram girl in Clue (1985) and Joan of Arc in Bill & Ted’s Excellent Adventure (1989).
In 1981 she co-wrote ‘Our Lips Are Sealed’ with Terry Hall of Fun Boy Three and the Specials.

5BvJzeQpmsdsFp4HGUYUEx.name: Vampire Weekend
f: The band is named after a student film Ezra Koenig abandoned after two days; years later he edited the footage into a two-minute trailer.
Spin named them ‘The Year’s Best New Band’ in March 2008, the first band shot for its cover before releasing a debut album.
They self-produced their debut album while working full-time, Chris Tomson as a music archivist and Ezra Koenig as a middle-school English teacher.
The band grew out of a rap collaboration, ‘L’Homme Run’, between Ezra Koenig, Chris Tomson and Koenig’s roommate at Columbia University.
In January 2012, Barack Obama added them to a short list of artists, with Jay-Z, John Legend and Alicia Keys, whose support he sought for re-election.

6IpcPRU1kV0J58kd2w8vSC.name: Dwight Twilley Band
f: Dwight Twilley and Phil Seymour met in Tulsa in 1967, at a cinema where they had both gone to see the Beatles’ A Hard Day’s Night.
By sheer chance, the first recording studio Dwight Twilley and Phil Seymour wandered into was Sun Studio.
They recorded ‘I’m on Fire’ in one night; it became their debut single and reached No. 16 in the US in 1975.
Shelter Records rejected their follow-up single, ‘Shark (in the Dark)’, after Jaws became a hit, apparently to avoid looking like a novelty act.

2h3ooJn8m8X8cL2g1BZ1Rd.name: Yard Act
f: The band’s James Smith says they ‘Trojan Horsed’ the scene Idles had opened up, using it for attention while always planning to subvert it and move away.
Their lyrics are ranted, not sung, and often take on capitalism, gentrification and social class with ‘dark humour and cynical storytelling’.
Their cited influences run from Sleaford Mods and the Fall to Sophie Ellis-Bextor, Manu Dibango and Glen Campbell.
James Smith, of Post War Glamour Girls, and Ryan Needham, of Menace Beach, formed the band in September 2019, after moving into a house together in Meanwood.
Their second album, Where’s My Utopia? (2024), was produced by Gorillaz member Remi Kabaka Jr.

244fcyNSuyhbRlMGfMbYrO.name: Badly Drawn Boy
f: Damon Gough took the name Badly Drawn Boy from a character in the TV show The Magic Ball, which he saw at a party in Trafford in 1995.
Q magazine put him among its 2002 ‘5 Bands That Could Go Either Way’, as he tended to tell long stories on stage instead of playing songs.
The track ‘I Love You All’ from his 1998 EP2 was also released on a music box playing eleven seconds of it, considered much rarer than the record.
His specialist subject on a celebrity edition of Mastermind in December 2015 was his music hero, Bruce Springsteen.
His first album, The Hour of Bewilderbeast, won the 2000 Mercury Music Prize, beating Doves to the £20,000 prize.

2cevwbv7ISD92VMNLYLHZA.name: Rilo Kiley
f: Blake Sennett once said the name Rilo Kiley came from a dream in which a sports almanac chased him and listed a 19th-century Australian rules footballer of that name.
Jenny Lewis wanted to call the band Love's Way, after her parents' lounge act in Las Vegas, but Blake Sennett ‘didn't go for it’.
Blake Sennett first asked Jenny Lewis to sing backing vocals in the band; she refused to join unless she could sing lead.
The band's Jenny Lewis acted in Baywatch and The Golden Girls, and Blake Sennett played Joey the Rat on Boy Meets World.
Dave Foley of The Kids in the Hall funded the band's debut EP, released in 1999.

3UkN1XeK2D4wD4uhtJx4vb.name: SUUNS
f: They recorded Hold/Still in Dallas in 2015 with John Congleton, who pushed them to capture flawless live takes of each track without overdubs.
With Jerusalem in My Heart, they recorded a joint album in a week in November 2012, mixing Eastern modes and Arabic vocals with their keyboard arpeggios and guitars.
The band began in mid-2007, when Ben Shemie and Joe Yarmush got together to make some beats that quickly turned into songs.
Their debut, Zeroes QC, co-produced by Jace Lasek of the Besnard Lakes, had a ‘rigorous strategy behind every gorgeous onslaught’, said a New York Times reviewer.
In 2016 they curated their own programme at Le Guess Who? festival in Utrecht, with performances by Pauline Oliveros and Alessandro Cortini.

3HQyFCFFfJO3KKBlUfZsyW.name: Randy Newman
f: He studied music at UCLA but dropped out one semester short of a BA; he finally completed his degree there in June 2021.
In 1970 Harry Nilsson recorded a whole album of his songs, Nilsson Sings Newman, with Newman on piano.
In the 1970s he co-wrote the ‘Most Original Soft Drink Ever’ jingle for Dr Pepper with Jake Holmes.
Three of his uncles, Alfred, Lionel and Emil Newman, were Hollywood film composers.
He has won two Academy Awards from 22 nominations, along with three Emmys and seven Grammys.

1r1uxoy19fzMxunt3ONAkG.name: Phoebe Bridgers
f: She vowed to cover ‘Iris’ if Donald Trump lost the 2020 election; her duet with Maggie Rogers, on Bandcamp for one day only, got 28,000 downloads.
Producer Tony Berg offered to make her first album for free after hearing ‘Waiting Room’, a song she wrote at 16.
An Apple commercial she made with her band Sloppy Jane gave her some financial security, so she planned to finish her first album before selling it to a label.
She took the part of Sally at two of Danny Elfman's concerts of The Nightmare Before Christmas soundtrack.
As a child she earned extra money busking at the Pasadena Farmers Market.

7HvQfRNJCvPXTVirKKB0Nn.name: Moondog
f: In 1954 he won a New York State Supreme Court case against the DJ Alan Freed, who had to stop using the nickname ‘Moondog’ on air.
By 1947 Louis Hardin had taken the name Moondog, after a dog ‘who used to howl at the moon more than any dog I knew of’.
He added a Viking-style horned helmet in the 1960s to avoid comparisons with Christ or a monk, and passers-by called him ‘the Viking of Sixth Avenue’.
He called his rhythm ‘snaketime’ and said: ‘I'm not gonna die in 4/4 time’.
Philip Glass and Steve Reich said they took his work very seriously, appreciating it ‘much more than what we were exposed to at Juilliard’.

6mcrZQmgzFGRWf7C0SObou.name: Frankie Valli & The Four Seasons
f: The Four Seasons named themselves after a New Jersey bowling alley in 1960, having just failed an audition for its lounge.
From 1965 to 1974, Frankie Valli's ‘solo’ records were cut with the Four Seasons in the same sessions, usually told apart by having no falsetto.
Vee-Jay pitted them against the Beatles on a two-record set, The Beatles vs the Four Seasons, which buyers could use to score individual recordings.
They released a cover of Bob Dylan's ‘Don't Think Twice, It's All Right’ under the name the Wonder Who?, and it went top 20.
Their first three Vee-Jay singles, Christmas record aside, made them the first rock band to top the Billboard singles chart three times in a row.

5ffMSKGQRhetAjBjEgkRun.name: DJ Mehdi
f: His 2006 mixtape Loukoums, a tribute to J Dilla modelled on Dilla's album Donuts, was first pressed in just 200 copies.
His 2006 album Lucky Boy was the first album on Ed Banger Records, the label founded by his friend Pedro Winter.
He and Pedro Winter hosted a very successful monthly night at the former Paris club Pulp.
He mixed hip hop with electronic music, working with Daft Punk, MC Solaar, Futura 2000, Asian Dub Foundation and Chromeo.
He belonged to ‘Club 75’, a circle of DJ friends including Cassius, Busy P and Xavier de Rosnay of Justice.

36E7oYfz3LLRto6l2WmDcD.name: Pulp
f: The band started as Arabicus, after a coffee bean in the Financial Times: Jarvis Cocker's first choice, the Michael Caine film title Pulp, was deemed too short.
Russell Senior, later the band's guitarist, recognised Jarvis Cocker from the charismatic sales technique Cocker used in his part-time job at the local fish market.
They recorded their 1987 album Freaks in one week, on a budget of £600.
Jarvis Cocker sought a £5,000 loan from his family to keep the release of the band's 1992 single ‘Babies’ on schedule.
They headlined Glastonbury's Pyramid Stage twice at their peak, and returned to it in 2025 as a surprise act.

0uAjBatvB4ubpd4kCfjmNt.name: A Flock Of Seagulls
f: The band were first called Level 7, but renamed themselves after The Stranglers' singer yelled ‘a flock of seagulls’ while they stood in the front row.
Their singer Mike Score's winged haircut reportedly began in Trinidad, when Frank Maudsley hurriedly pushed him from the mirror as he combed his hair back.
Mike Score was a hairdresser when he bought a second-hand Korg MS-10 synthesiser and formed the band with friends who had never played bass or drums.
They get a mention in Pulp Fiction: Samuel L. Jackson's character calls Burr Steers's character ‘flock of seagulls’ because of his hairstyle.
They won a Grammy Award in 1983 for their instrumental ‘D.N.A.’.

3g2qbrpTcYUxoDOQ610r3F.name: Wesley Gonzalez
f: He formed the north London DIY trio Let's Wrestle in 2005, at the age of 15, reportedly in a garden shed.
He said a cardboard cutout of Tony Wilson was kept out of shot throughout filming of his ‘A Taste of Something New’ video, to give it some authenticity.
He taught himself piano by learning to play Stevie Wonder and Al Green songs.
His album Excellent Musician came from unplanned, partly improvised recording sessions over four days spread across a few months.

6T1GNMxXuljv0C0ZRR60CC.name: Rose Elinor Dougall
f: As a student, she appeared uncredited on BBC Two's James May's Top Toys, drawing the presenter on an Etch A Sketch.
She joined The Pipettes in 2003 after Monster Bobby introduced her at the Basketmakers pub in Brighton, and sang lead on ‘Judy’ and ‘Dirty Mind’.
She sang and played on Mark Ronson and the Business Intl's album Record Collection, and co-wrote its closing song, ‘The Night Last Night’.
In November 2016 she performed with the Royal Ballet at the Royal Opera House, in Wayne McGregor's Carbon Life.
She is the granddaughter of the BBC news broadcaster Robert Dougall.

5Q8NEHGX70m1kkojbtm8wa.name: Ibeyi
f: Ibeyi means ‘twins’ in Yoruba, and the twin sisters Lisa-Kaindé Díaz and Naomi Díaz sing in English, French, Spanish and Yoruba.
The duo's Naomi Díaz learned the cajón at 11, after the death in 2006 of her father, the Buena Vista Social Club percussionist Anga Díaz.
In the video for their single ‘River’, the twins take turns having their heads forced underwater while the other sings.
In 2016 they appeared in the film for Beyoncé's Lemonade, as members of a farm utopia that offers a safe space for black women.
XL Recordings owner Richard Russell was the only other contributor to their 2015 debut album.

5W10uJRsbt9bROJDKoI1Wn.name: Moses Sumney
f: He moved with his family to Ghana at 10 and grew up on a goat farm in Accra, commuting to school by public bus.
He wrote a cappella music for years, didn't learn an instrument until he was older, and didn't perform his songs in public until he was 20.
He recorded his first EP, Mid-City Island (2014), on a four-track recorder given to him by Dave Sitek of TV on the Radio.
In 2014 record labels took notice of him in Los Angeles; he turned them down and moved to Asheville, North Carolina.
In 2025 he played the clown Feste in a Shakespeare in the Park production of Twelfth Night.

7bcbShaqKdcyjnmv4Ix8j6.name: St. Vincent
f: Annie Clark took the name St. Vincent from a Nick Cave song that mentions the hospital where Dylan Thomas died; it was also her great-grandmother's middle name.
She spent some of her teenage years working as a roadie for her aunt and uncle, the guitar-vocal jazz duo Tuck & Patti.
She named her debut album, Marry Me, after a line from the sitcom Arrested Development.
She began writing her second album, Actor, on her computer using GarageBand, because neighbours had complained about the noise.
She co-wrote Taylor Swift's Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 ‘Cruel Summer’.

59pWgeY26Q6yJy37QvJflh.name: Sleigh Bells
f: Derek Miller was working at a Brazilian bistro in Brooklyn when Alexis Krauss dined there with her mother, who volunteered her as the singer he wanted.
Alexis Krauss was pursuing a Rhodes Scholarship when she met Derek Miller, but chose to form the band with him instead.
Before the band, Alexis Krauss performed in the teen pop group RubyBlue from age 12 to 16, and later taught Spanish at an elementary school in the Bronx.
M.I.A. signed them to her label, N.E.E.T. Recordings, after Derek Miller worked with her on the track ‘Meds and Feds’ in 2009.
The name Sleigh Bells comes from the phrase Derek Miller used to label CD-Rs of his demos.

5hAhrnb0Ch4ODwWu4tsbpi.name: Yo La Tengo
f: Yo La Tengo are named after a 1962 New York Mets story that ends with left fielder Frank Thomas asking Richie Ashburn, ‘What the hell is a yellow tango?’
On their first LP, Ride the Tiger (1986), Ira Kaplan was credited with ‘naive guitar’.
James McNew joined the band as a fill-in bassist, and on an early European tour left the box of merchandise EPs behind at a club in Münster.
They played an anonymous stand-in for the Velvet Underground in the 1996 film I Shot Andy Warhol.
In 2001 they recorded a score for eight short undersea documentaries by Jean Painlevé, called The Sounds of the Sounds of Science.

7jefIIksOi1EazgRTfW2Pk.name: Electric Light Orchestra
f: Their first album was called No Answer in the US after a record company secretary, unable to reach the UK label for its title, left that note.
Jeff Lynne turned down an invitation for the band to headline Knebworth in August 1979, which let Led Zeppelin headline instead.
They have the most Billboard Hot 100 Top 40 hits without a No. 1, with 20; their only UK No. 1 was ‘Xanadu’, with Olivia Newton-John.
Electric Light Orchestra's name is a pun on electric light and the ‘light orchestral music’ played on the BBC Light Programme.
They played their first concert on 16 April 1972, at the Greyhound pub in Croydon.

0oKYiTD5CdNbrofRvM1dIr.name: Alice Coltrane
f: In the mid-1970s she took the monastic name Turiyasangitananda, which she translated as ‘the Transcendental Lord's Highest Song of Bliss’.
She studied jazz with Bud Powell in Paris, where she worked as the intermission pianist at the Blue Note Jazz Club in 1960.
Steve ‘Flying Lotus’ Ellison, her grandnephew, sampled her harp from ‘Blue Nile’ for his 2010 tribute to her, ‘Drips//Auntie's Harp’.
Doja Cat spent part of her adolescence at Alice Coltrane's ashram.

55tLEUlrzGNtACuMVJZHNf.name: Peter Ivers
f: He played harmonica; at a 1968 concert, Muddy Waters called him “the greatest harp player alive”.
He opened for Fleetwood Mac at Los Angeles's Universal Amphitheatre in 1976 wearing nothing but a diaper.
He scored David Lynch's 1977 film Eraserhead and wrote and sang its ‘In Heaven (Lady in the Radiator Song)’.
He was born Peter Scott Rose; his mother chose the surname Ivers out of the phone book when she remarried.
He hosted New Wave Theatre, the first chance for many alternative rock musicians to reach a national TV audience; Dead Kennedys and Fear both appeared.

0SrIPejckovMwhrN3MZFPB.name: Daisy the Great
f: The duo began when Kelley Dugan and Mina Walker met at acting school and, in Walker's words, were “kind of pretending to be a band”.
Recording the claps for ‘Time Machine’, they stood in a circle clapping, then found the sound was better if they all smacked their own backsides.
Their third EP, released in 2024, is called Spectacle: Daisy the Great vs. Tony Visconti.
They have opened for the Indigo Girls and Samia, and toured with The Kooks and The Vaccines.

6s22t5Y3prQHyaHWUN1R1C.name: AJR
f: In November 2012 Ryan Met tweeted the band's debut single, ‘I'm Ready’, to about 80 celebrities; one of them, Sia, told her manager about it.
They started out in 2005 as TB3, short for Tapping Brothers to the Third Power, street performing in New York City's parks.
Their debut single, ‘I'm Ready’, samples SpongeBob SquarePants singing his catchphrase in the cartoon's first episode.
Jack Met said in 2017 that the band's YouTube cover of the Lumineers' ‘Ho Hey’ inspired Shawn Mendes to perform covers of his own.
They played ‘Bummerland’ at We the People, the virtual concert for Joe Biden's inauguration, on 17 January 2021.

3JsMj0DEzyWc0VDlHuy9Bx.name: Supertramp
f: Supertramp first called themselves Daddy. To avoid confusion with “Daddy Longlegs”, they renamed themselves after William Henry Davies's book The Autobiography of a Super-Tramp.
On the band's 1970 Norway trip, the first gig, on 30 December, was on top of a mountain, and most of the audience arrived on skis.
Dutch millionaire Stanley August Miesegaes bankrolled them, having offered Rick Davies, a former bandmate of Gilbert O'Sullivan, the chance to form his own band.
Their original lyricist, Richard Palmer, later wrote lyrics for King Crimson under the name Richard Palmer-James.
Canada was their biggest market, where Crime of the Century and Breakfast in America were both certified diamond.

04XggbrM51GcFPTxBYtRXT.name: Rostam
f: He was 26 when he produced Vampire Weekend's Contra, his first No. 1 album.
He produced Vampire Weekend's debut album shortly after graduating, while working several full-time jobs at the same time.
He composed the music for both seasons of The OA, the TV series made by his brother, Zal Batmanglij.
He won a Grammy for Vampire Weekend's Modern Vampires of the City and was nominated for Album of the Year for producing Haim's Women in Music Pt. III.
He wrote original music for Kenneth Lonergan's play This Is Our Youth, starring Michael Cera and Kieran Culkin, on Broadway in 2014.

7bU9pQZvphKhzJy9x6DvQD.name: Sun Drug
f: The band's members played the Los Angeles circuit for a few years as Vanaprasta, then reinvented themselves under the counsel of indie musician Rocco DeLuca, their “musical shaman”.
After spending much of a year workshopping with Rocco DeLuca, they started from scratch and recorded a batch of new songs in Collin Desha's home studio.
Working with Rocco DeLuca taught them how to capture live ambience in their recordings.
The band's four members are Collin Desha, Taylor Brown, Cameron Dmytryk and Steven Wilkin.

0IecGJbdBeYSOVtSPRehh5.name: Billy Preston
f: The Beatles credited their 1969 single ‘Get Back’ to “The Beatles with Billy Preston”, the only co-performer credit they gave after they began recording as independent artists.
When John Lennon proposed that Billy Preston join the Beatles, Paul McCartney countered that it was hard enough reaching agreement with four.
Dick Clark liked Billy Preston's ‘Space Race’ so much that he used it for American Bandstand's mid-show break for virtually the rest of the show's run.
Aged 11, he sang ‘Blueberry Hill’ with Nat King Cole on Cole's NBC TV show.
He was the first artist to record George Harrison's ‘My Sweet Lord’, on his 1970 album Encouraging Words.

2XKBOnP3qXHP2FpzKplAYh.name: Michael Johnson
f: He spent a year in the Chad Mitchell Trio, co-writing with John Denver; the group was renamed Denver, Boise & Johnson.
His music studies at college were cut short when he won an international talent contest whose first prize included an Epic Records deal.
In 1966 he went to Barcelona's Liceu Conservatory to study with the classical guitarists Graciano and Renata Tarragó.
When his trio with John Denver ended, he took a major supporting role off-Broadway in Jacques Brel Is Alive and Well and Living in Paris.
He had two No. 1 country hits, 1986's ‘Give Me Wings’ and ‘The Moon Is Still Over Her Shoulder’.

5MWBg16f5UYiaSlyVhzlIW.name: John Cale
f: On TV's I've Got a Secret, his secret was playing an 18-hour concert; Karl Schenzer's was being the only audience member who stayed throughout.
Lou Reed reportedly told Robert Quine that John Cale's ideas were too out there, such as recording the Velvet Underground's next album with the amplifiers underwater.
The Velvet Underground's first commercially available recording, ‘Loop’, given away with Aspen magazine, was a feedback experiment written and conducted by him.
He insisted on working with Nick Drake, and played viola and harpsichord on ‘Fly’ and piano, organ and celesta on ‘Northern Sky’.
After he shopped a Velvet Underground demo tape around Britain in 1965, David Bowie and the Yardbirds covered the band's songs before its debut album came out.

546WiMGysEqWZTzP8hJvB2.name: Mickey Avalon
f: After Mickey Avalon was booed off stage opening for the Red Hot Chili Peppers in Oklahoma City, John Frusciante wrote to fans there accusing them of lacking ‘regard for humanity’.
Former MTV VJ Simon Rex befriended him in Los Angeles, encouraged him to rap, and passed out demos with him to Hollywood clubs.
His rap group the Dyslexic Speedreaders included Simon ‘Dirt Nasty’ Rex, Andre Legacy, Avalon’s friend since elementary school, and Beardo, a friend from modelling.
Born Yeshe Perl, he first rapped under the stage name the Relevant when he entered hip-hop in 2000.
His ‘What Do You Say?’, on the soundtrack of The Hangover, was announced as the last song the Dyslexic Speedreaders would release.

5v4XGACPGcMZs2ANXBzVmC.name: Liz Lawrence
f: After touring with Bombay Bicycle Club, she spent about six months in an empty flat with just a bed, a chair and a saucepan, listening to Sun Ra alone.
She spent a few years teaching herself to produce, until she was good enough to make her own music ‘on her own terms’.
Q magazine compared her favourably to Florence and the Machine and called her ‘a starlet in the making’.
Her debut album, Bedroom Hero (2012), collected sweet folk-pop songs she had written as a teenager.
Besides her solo work, she is half of the electro-pop duo Cash+David.

7FIoB5PHdrMZVC3q2HE5MS.name: George Harrison
f: He impressed John Lennon by playing the lead guitar part of ‘Raunchy’ on the upper deck of a Liverpool bus.
While pregnant with him, his mother Louise Harrison tuned in to Radio India every Sunday, hoping the sitars and tablas would calm her baby.
The Beatles' first Hamburg residency ended early when he was deported for being too young to work in nightclubs.
He called himself ‘Carl Harrison’, after Carl Perkins, on his group’s first tour of Scotland in 1960.
He co-founded HandMade Films in 1978, initially to produce the Monty Python film Life of Brian.

3lmR0qMiGuoIF9UC54egcG.name: Aldous Harding
f: She was busking outside a Geraldine bakery to afford a ticket to Anika Moa's gig when Moa threw in money and asked her to open it.
She told the New Zealand magazine Under the Radar she liked the sound of the name Aldous, a bit like a ‘manly Alice’.
To make the video for ‘Blend’, she had an outfit made and spent about eight hours dancing on a lazy susan.
She narrowly lost the APRA Silver Scroll to Lorde with ‘Horizon’, then won it in 2019 with ‘The Barrel’.
She made her recording debut at 13, singing ‘Exactly What to Say’, a song she wrote with her mother, folk singer Lorina Harding.

4fFSyYQa0jRwFSunVahGw8.name: TTRRUUCES
f: Natalie Findlay and Jules Apollinaire first met in summer 2014, started hanging out because both lived on Broadway Market in East London, and formed the band in 2019.
They left London for France for a year to immerse themselves in making their debut album.
Natalie Findlay said the band ‘got completely carried away’ with their debut album ‘and made it into a rock opera’.
Natalie Findlay also records solo as Findlay; her song ‘Off & On’ featured in a BMW advert that premiered during the 2014 Winter Olympics.

0jOs0wnXCu1bGGP7kh5uIu.name: Tim Maia
f: He and Jorge Ben were both nicknamed ‘Babulina’ for their enthusiastic pronunciation of Ronnie Self's rockabilly song ‘Bop-A-Lena’.
In Tijuca, he taught guitar to other children, including his friends Roberto Carlos and Erasmo Esteves.
He had a hit re-recording Lulu Santos's ‘Como uma Onda’ for a TV advert, and Santos returned the favour by recording Maia's ‘Descobridor dos Sete Mares’.
Angry at how his publisher split royalties, he set up his own, Seroma, named from the first syllables of his first, middle and last names.
He was the second youngest of nineteen children and began writing melodies at the age of eight.

5mFKYdmiYwNJTDtSzgFyQx.name: Andy Shauf
f: He played almost every instrument on his 2016 album The Party himself; only the strings, written and played by Colin Nealis, were someone else's.
His 2023 album Norm is a concept album that follows a stalker.
He played Christian music with his parents and was the drummer in the Christian pop punk band Captain until 2006.
His parents ran an electronics and music store, giving him access to a variety of instruments; he plays guitar, drums and clarinet.
His band Foxwarren, with D. A. Kissick, Avery Kissick and Dallas Bryson, earned a Juno nomination for its 2018 debut album.

64RBScSzzcUegqlm1nqZgK.name: Johnny Parry
f: He founded Lost Toys Records and has played with Beth Orton, Talvin Singh and the Turner Prize-winning artist Martin Creed.
His An Anthology of All Things (2017) has eight movements, with lyrics built from short statements submitted by the local community.
The Arts Desk described his voice as ‘a growled whisper that occasionally expands into a Bowie-esque croon’.
For Folk's Sake wrote that he was staking ‘his claim to be the UK's very own Sufjan Stevens’.

0fA0VVWsXO9YnASrzqfmYu.name: Kid Cudi
f: Working at New York's BAPE store, he forgot to remove a sensor from a jacket Kanye West had bought and had to chase him down in SoHo.
He met his future mentor Kanye West in a Virgin Megastore in 2006, after spotting ‘the gleam of a Jesus piece’ out of the corner of his eye.
His single ‘Make Her Say’, which samples Lady Gaga's ‘Poker Face’, was originally titled ‘I Poke Her Face’.
He met David Guetta while making a cameo in the Black Eyed Peas' ‘I Gotta Feeling’ video, and the pair went on to record the hit ‘Memories’.
He left Cleveland in 2005 with $500 and a demo tape, and moved in with his uncle, jazz drummer Kalil Madi, in the South Bronx.

0dU2EKM6vca3xmJ9kl8zoI.name: Blue Sky Black Death
f: Blue Sky Black Death's name is ‘a skydiving phrase alluding to beauty and death’.
Their album with Ceschi, Deadpan Darling, was shelved when most of its final mixes were lost on a crashed hard drive; it finally emerged in 2021.
After an online petition from fans, Babygrande released the instrumentals from their album with the rapper Holocaust on vinyl and CD.
In December 2017 they posted on Twitter that the duo was ‘resting eternally’.
The duo were the producers Ryan Maguire, known as Kingston, and Ian Taggart, known as Young God and later Televangel.

27DCwiPx5ocQsf4K43SlIL.name: Colin Blunstone
f: Rod Argent heard him singing a Ricky Nelson song to himself in a corner and offered a deal: if Blunstone sang lead, Argent would play keyboards.
He was first recruited to the Zombies as a rhythm guitarist, and turned up to his first rehearsal with two black eyes from playing rugby.
In 2006 Neil Tennant of Pet Shop Boys called him ‘the missing link between Dusty Springfield and Nick Drake’.
He worked in the burglary claims section of the Sun Alliance insurance company between the Zombies and his solo career.
In 1969 he released three singles under the pseudonym Neil MacArthur, including a remake of the Zombies' ‘She's Not There’ that charted in the UK.

60nDKjd690Luygtd3Fm0Cu.name: Ogi
f: PJ Morton reposted her cover of his song ‘Alright’, which caught the attention of No I.D., who signed her to his Def Jam imprint ARTium in 2021.
Her grandmother often woke her at sunrise by singing Nigerian hymns, the first songs Ogi remembers memorising.
She discovered she had perfect pitch while singing in her high school's jazz choir.
She majored in political science and minored in legal studies at Northwestern University, where she sang in an a cappella group, THUNK.

6XiSck3QPuXk7ho6zlDz3P.name: The Bees
f: In their video for ‘Chicken Payback’, set in a Japanese arcade, a rock and roll dance diva dances so quickly that his shoes catch fire.
Their ‘Chicken Payback’ launched Age UK's 2011 ‘Thank You’ campaign, performed in the advert by 81-year-old Joy Graham with a jazz orchestra.
Their cover of ‘A Minha Menina’, an Os Mutantes track originally by Jorge Ben, was used in adverts for Citroën and Magners cider.
The band, from Ventnor on the Isle of Wight and known in the US as A Band of Bees, were Mercury-nominated for their 2002 debut, Sunshine Hit Me.
In November 2025 they launched a Kickstarter to fund Sonic Sunshine – Stories from The Bees, a documentary about the band.

5CzlICF8GCY0pRC82MKrhX.name: Labi Siffre
f: At first he refused Dr. Dre and Eminem a sample for ‘My Name Is’, objecting to homophobic and misogynistic lyrics, and agreed after hearing only the clean version.
In 2025, more than 50 years after its release, his album track ‘Bless the Telephone’ went viral; by 2026 it was his most-streamed song, with over 100 million streams.
He said his anti-apartheid song ‘(Something Inside) So Strong’ took 18 months to get recorded because nobody wanted to touch it; it reached No. 4 in the UK.
He appears as a violin player in the video for Madness's 1981 cover of his ‘It Must Be Love’, which reached No. 4 in the UK.
In 1978 he tried to represent the UK at Eurovision with ‘Solid Love’, which placed fifth of the 12 songs in A Song for Europe.

6PBv8t9YTLggA9ZMwpeoqj.name: Joan As Police Woman
f: Joan Wasser named Joan As Police Woman after the TV series Police Woman, finding Angie Dickinson ‘really powerful but sexy at the same time’ in the role.
She was a member of Antony and the Johnsons and contributed to their Mercury Prize-winning album I Am a Bird Now.
She is a member of Iggy Pop's touring band and performs with Damon Albarn's Africa Express.
In late 1997 she formed the band Black Beetle with the remaining members of Jeff Buckley's band.

42WJFNdxsAgcn9PfjT61Z3.name: Eleanor Friedberger
f: She is one half of the Fiery Furnaces with her older brother, Matthew Friedberger, and sings most of the band's vocals.
Spoon's ‘Anything You Want’ and Franz Ferdinand's ‘Eleanor Put Your Boots On’ were both written about her.
She filmed the video for ‘In Between Stars’ herself, with help from Kim Gordon, formerly of Sonic Youth.
She grew up singing in a Greek Orthodox church with her grandmother, Olga Sarantos, and her family.
Her brother, Matthew Friedberger, dedicated his 2006 solo album, Winter Women, to her.

6LWofoi18999gZK0EgVSjv.name: Tess Henley
f: In 2014 the producer Don Was picked her as grand prize winner of Guitar Center Singer-Songwriter III, the competition's first female winner.
She made her TV debut on Jimmy Kimmel Live! in January 2015, then played eight showcases in three days at the Sundance Film Festival.
In December 2020 she featured on ‘Funny Seeing You Here’ from Jack Harlow's album Thats What They All Say.
In 2025 she scored the short film Terror Keeps You Slender, with songs from Leon Michels of El Michels Affair; it premiered at the Tribeca Festival.
She graduated as valedictorian of Kentlake High School in 2006, having played basketball and soccer year-round.

23EA28263XvtIrXuySX6oI.name: Francis and the Lights
f: Francis Farewell Starlite drove across the US in a decommissioned postal truck to New York City, where he formed the band.
Francis Farewell Starlite invented the ‘Prismizer’ vocal effect, heard on Frank Ocean's ‘Close to You’ and throughout Chance the Rapper's Coloring Book.
Instead of signing a record deal, Francis Farewell Starlite incorporated the band as a company in 2008; a $100,000 investment valued it at $1 million.
Born Abe Morre Katz-Milder, Francis Farewell Starlite changed his name legally in 2004; asked why, he paused for a minute before answering.
The ‘and the Lights’ in the band's name refers both to the lights on a stage and to the pixels on a computer screen.

2kTZfKGZEj8R76z3ooKOF1.name: Your Smith
f: As a teenager, she sang in her bathroom pretending to be on First Avenue's main stage; she later sold out the Minneapolis venue.
At 16, she was playing Zorbaz Pizza restaurants in Minnesota and opened for B. B. King in Duluth and Rochester.
In 2010 she and Jesse Schuster released Live at the Cedar, hand-packaged with an envelope, string and wax stamp; it sold out within six months.
In 2014 she released a single with Lizzo called ‘Let 'em Say’.
Your Smith is Caroline Smith, who fronted the indie folk band Caroline Smith and the Good Night Sleeps before signing to Neon Gold Records as Your Smith in 2018.

7nwUJBm0HE4ZxD3f5cy5ok.name: Aretha Franklin
f: In the 1960s at Chicago's Regal Theater, radio host Pervis Spann announced she should be crowned ‘the Queen of Soul’ and put a crown on her head.
She won the first eight Grammy Awards given for Best Female R&B Vocal Performance, from 1968 to 1975.
Berry Gordy asked her and her elder sister Erma Franklin to sign to his Tamla label, but their father, C. L. Franklin, refused, feeling it wasn't yet established.
In 1987 she became the first female artist inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
In 2019 she was given a posthumous Pulitzer Prize special citation for her contribution to American music and culture over more than five decades.

2AV6XDIs32ofIJhkkDevjm.name: Curtis Mayfield
f: He played boogie-woogie piano in F-sharp, all on the black keys, and Jerry Butler said tuning his guitar that way gave him his unique sound.
He got his first guitar at ten, and later recalled loving it so much that he used to sleep with it.
His Super Fly spent four weeks at number one and is a rare soundtrack that outsold the film it was taken from.
Barack Obama walked on for his keynote speech at the 2004 Democratic Convention to ‘Keep On Pushing’, by Curtis Mayfield's group the Impressions.
He wrote ‘People Get Ready’ for the Impressions in 1965; Rolling Stone ranked it 24th of the 500 Greatest Songs of All Time in 2004.

5QdyldG4Fl4TPiOIeMNpBZ.name: Big Thief
f: Drummer James Krivchenia first joined the band as its sound engineer, then replaced founding drummer Jason Burger.
NPR's Bob Boilen said he couldn't recall the last time one band had made his top five two years running, as they did with Masterpiece and Capacity.
Their live bassist Joshua Crumbly went to Juilliard and, Buck Meek says, still takes private lessons from Ron Carter.
Before forming the band in 2015, Adrianne Lenker and Buck Meek met at a show in Boston, met again in Brooklyn and began performing as a duo.
On 22 August 2026 they debuted Horsepower, a triple album featuring Lucinda Williams, Gillian Welch and Iris DeMent, at Nashville's Ryman Auditorium.

1Pag7p4HbSdZIDzgNLsk39.name: Fanny
f: They were the first all-female band to release a full-length album on a major label.
June Millington wanted a band name with a girl's name in it, like Fanny Brice's, and said ‘we didn't know what Fanny meant in England, not at all’.
David Bowie wrote to them admiring their work and showed them mime techniques at a post-show party.
They played on Barbra Streisand's 1971 albums Stoney End and Barbra Joan Streisand, because Streisand wanted to record with a small band.
Their biggest hit, ‘Butter Boy’, written by Jean Millington about David Bowie, reached number 29 on the Billboard Hot 100 in April 1975, by which time the band had split.

3RyJG8xp58XSmsiuIySzUj.name: Adam Green
f: His great-grandmother Felice Bauer was engaged to Franz Kafka.
His film The Wrong Ferarri was shot entirely on iPhone, with Macaulay Culkin, Pete Doherty and Devendra Banhart in the cast.
Until Jacket Full of Danger in 2006, every one of his albums had been released on the 22nd of the month.
His Moldy Peaches duet with Kimya Dawson, ‘Anyone Else But You’, was featured in the film Juno.
His song ‘Jessica’ is about the singer Jessica Simpson.

5ROABVYKJnEJa7ilOwceaq.name: Binki Shapiro
f: She made a 2008 album as Little Joy with Strokes drummer Fabrizio Moretti and singer Rodrigo Amarante; Interview magazine called it an alt-pop gem.
Adam Green was the support act when her band Little Joy toured Brazil, where, he said, they ‘are really huge’.
Adam Green recalled meeting her over a meal at a Mexican restaurant: ‘It wasn't that eventful.’
She played some shows with Adam Green while he was taking time off from making music to work as an artist and filmmaker.

2rc78XDH9zuJP6bm78lU8Z.name: Derek & The Dominos
f: Worried the public didn't know Eric Clapton was in the band, the record labels Atco and Polydor handed out badges reading ‘Derek is Eric’.
Eric Clapton recalls that pianist Tony Ashton suggested ‘Del and the Dominos’, having taken to calling him ‘Derek’ or ‘Del’ on the Delaney & Bonnie tour.
On a UK club tour, they charged £1 admission, and venue contracts banned using Eric Clapton's name as a crowd-puller.
The recording of George Harrison's All Things Must Pass marked their formation, and Harrison took part in their first session as a band.
Their ‘Layla’ was released in 1970 but didn't reach the top ten in the US and UK until March 1972.

3DiDSECUqqY1AuBP8qtaIa.name: Alicia Keys
f: At four, she made her acting debut on The Cosby Show, as Maria, one of Rudy's slumber-party friends.
She wrote her first song, about her late grandfather, by the age of 12, inspired by the film Philadelphia.
When she was ten, a neighbourhood friend who was moving gave her family an old upright piano.
Born in Manhattan's Hell's Kitchen, she wrote, composed and co-produced her first Broadway musical, Hell's Kitchen, which won two Tony Awards.
Her Unplugged (2005) made her the first female artist to have an MTV Unplugged project debut at number one on the Billboard 200.

55LHFEtIplWhsfyWZUwkf4.name: Foxygen
f: Jonathan Rado and Sam France started the band in high school, aged 14, and their early music won Agoura High School's Battle of the Bands.
In 2011 the producer Richard Swift ‘discovered’ them after they handed him one of their EPs at a Mynabirds show in New York.
Their 2017 album Hang is said to be the first they recorded in a studio; everything before it had been made at home.
In August 2022 the duo suggested on Instagram that they had broken up, but they played a brief reunion show at Zebulon in Los Angeles on 19 December 2023.

5gl6pfPwJ1coivVUMZPiS9.name: Dennis Wilson
f: He was the Beach Boys' drummer and the only dedicated surfer in the group.
Brian Wilson wrote the Beach Boys' debut record, ‘Surfin'’, at Dennis's urging, and Dennis recalled running down the street screaming that they were on the radio.
His raucous behaviour led other kids to nickname him ‘Dennis the Menace’, neighbourhood friend David Marks said.
He is sometimes cited as an uncredited writer of ‘You Are So Beautiful’, a 1974 hit for Joe Cocker that Wilson often sang in concert.
He co-starred in the 1971 film Two-Lane Blacktop, his only acting role.

1bdAJUX6JPsnYHbTl5jbk6.name: Joan Armatrading
f: She taught herself on a £3 guitar her mother got from a pawn shop in exchange for two prams.
She lost her first job, as a typist and comptometer operator, after taking her guitar to work and playing it during tea-breaks.
She thanked Elkie Brooks in the sleeve notes of Back to the Night, because Brooks had cooked for her and the band in the studio.
Her 2007 album Into the Blues entered the US Billboard Blues Chart at number one, a first for a UK female artist.
Her first classical work, Symphony No. 1, was premiered by the Chineke! Orchestra at London's Southbank Centre on 24 November 2023.

2GVyv9OLNp6cmxfUDbGrXM.name: Jack Nitzsche
f: He was credited on Rolling Stones records with the ‘Nitzsche-phone’; Andrew Loog Oldham later admitted inventing it for a piano or organ miked differently.
His instrumental ‘The Last Race’, heard in the 1965 film Village of the Giants, was used over 40 years later to open Quentin Tarantino's Death Proof.
As Phil Spector's arranger and conductor, he orchestrated the Wall of Sound on almost all Spector's hits, perhaps best heard on Ike and Tina Turner's ‘River Deep, Mountain High’.
He wrote the choral arrangements for the Rolling Stones' ‘You Can't Always Get What You Want’ and introduced the band to slide guitarist Ry Cooder in 1968.
He won an Academy Award in 1983 for co-writing ‘Up Where We Belong’, from An Officer and a Gentleman, with Will Jennings and Buffy Sainte-Marie.

6s92YZUPkTK1HL1WIGrPKE.name: Patrick Wolf
f: After leaving Universal, he told NME on 10 December 2008 that he would sell £10 shares in his next album through bandstocks.com.
A fan of Kenickie, he appeared as an extra in their music video for ‘Nightlife’ in 1997.
Fat Cat Records gave him an Atari computer and a mixing console after his writing and recordings caught its attention.
In 2013 he played the last dates of Patti Smith's Banga tour on Celtic harp and viola.
On 22 August 2026 he won second prize in both the cucumber and aubergine categories of the Ramsgate Horticultural Society's summer competition.

6SOQFIN80ymdMZAg8LmQ3n.name: Gwyneth Herbert
f: As the jazz duo Black Coffee, she and Will Rutter won a Polish television music competition after meeting a former Boney M member who was judging it.
Blue Note picked up her Between Me and the Wardrobe, recorded in three days and never meant for general release, making her its first UK signing in 30 years.
Her ‘Lovely London Town’, from her musical about Phyllis Pearsall creating the London A–Z street atlas, won the 2010 Stiles and Drewe Song of the Year Award.
She wrote the songs for Bristol Old Vic's 2022 Christmas show The Nutcracker and played what The Observer called its ‘terrifying, curse-hurling Queen Mouse’.
At 14 she recorded a demo tape of her own songs and drew music-industry interest, but chose to carry on with her studies.

3ceQN2NVlLg1hgTzljDE4n.name: Half Moon Run
f: Devon Portielje joined the band after answering Conner Molander and Dylan Phillips's Craigslist ad for a bassist or drummer, though he was neither.
They wrote ‘Shadows of Night’, released on 31 October 2025, for the soundtrack of the fourth season of The Witcher.
Their ‘Full Circle’ was used in a 2013 trailer for Ubisoft's Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag.
In May and June 2020 they performed together over video conference, then released the recordings as an album, The Covideo Sessions.
Their third album, A Blemish in the Great Light, won Adult Alternative Album of the Year at the 2020 Juno Awards.

4Bb8rhvCjLOjNOl1DbFkph.name: Loney dear
f: Signing Emil Svanängen to Real World Records in 2017, Peter Gabriel said Loney dear ‘may be Europe's answer to Brian Wilson’.
He recorded his 2003 debut, The Year of River Fontana, in his parents' basement in Jönköping with a minidisc microphone, and sold it on home-made CD-Rs.
His first major release came in February 2007, when Sub Pop reissued his album Loney, Noir in the US.
In 2009 he joined Andrew Bird on the tour for Bird's album Noble Beast.
He appears on ‘This Boy’, from I'm From Barcelona's 2006 album Let Me Introduce My Friends.

3nFkdlSjzX9mRTtwJOzDYB.name: JAŸ-Z
f: Big Daddy Kane used to bring him and Positive K out to freestyle on stage while Kane went off to change outfits.
He wrote The Blueprint in just two days; in 2019 the Library of Congress chose it for preservation in the National Recording Registry.
With no major-label deal, he sold burned CDs out of his car, and with Damon ‘Dame’ Dash and Kareem ‘Biggs’ Burke set up Roc-A-Fella Records.
Shawn Carter, known as ‘Jazzy’ around the neighbourhood, took the stage name Jay-Z in homage to his mentor Jaz-O.
His Vol. 2... Hard Knock Life won a Grammy, but he boycotted the ceremony over DMX's missing nomination and the academy's refusal to broadcast urban music categories.

5K4W6rqBFWDnAN6FQUkS6x.name: Kanye West
f: At 10, he moved to Nanjing, China, with his mother, Donda West, a Fulbright Scholar teaching at Nanjing University; she said he was the only foreigner in his class.
Inspired by Portishead's Roseland NYC Live, made with the New York Philharmonic Orchestra, he brought string arrangements into his hip-hop, hiring a string orchestra for Late Registration.
Labels including Capitol turned him down for lacking a gangsta image; Roc-A-Fella's Damon Dash signed him reluctantly, to stop him defecting elsewhere.
He was the first rapper to top the Billboard Hot 100 across three decades, from ‘Slow Jamz’ in 2003 to ‘Carnival’ in 2024.
His first official production credits came at 19, on eight tracks of Chicago rapper Grav's 1996 debut album, Down to Earth.

4wo1267SJuUfHgasdlfNfc.name: The Raconteurs
f: Playing ‘Store Bought Bones’ on Later with Jools Holland in November 2006, they needed four takes after Jack White's guitar malfunctioned; the broadcast was edited from all four.
In Australia The Raconteurs are The Saboteurs: a Queensland band already had the name and held out for more money than the record company would pay.
The band grew from Jack White and Brendan Benson writing ‘Steady, As She Goes’ together in an attic in the middle of a hot summer.
The intro and ending of their ‘Steady, As She Goes’ are often used to play out Saturday Live on BBC Radio 4.
They were the only act on Radio 1: Established 1967 both to cover a song, The Undertones' ‘Teenage Kicks’, and to be covered, by Corinne Bailey Rae.

3ZXXJ9nO1Dn9B0AJ25eAQY.name: Hamilton Leithauser
f: As a teenager, he had a summer job at Inner Ear Studios in Arlington, Virginia, where he helped engineer Fugazi's Red Medicine.
He had forgotten recording one of his shows at the Carlyle until he found it on a hard drive, one reason he released Live at Café Carlyle in 2020.
One summer as a young man, he worked as a museum security guard in New York, standing through countless three-hour shifts.
‘In a Blackout’, by him and former Vampire Weekend member Rostam Batmanglij, was used in Apple's commercial for the iPhone 7.
He and Peter Bauer formed The Walkmen after their Boston band, The Recoys, broke up; The Walkmen later rerecorded three Recoys songs.

7MhMgCo0Bl0Kukl93PZbYS.name: Blur
f: When Graham Coxon and Alex James missed a lip-synced performance on Italian TV in February 1996, they were replaced by a cardboard cut-out and a roadie.
Food Records disliked the band's original name, Seymour, so the group picked Blur from a list of alternatives the label drew up.
The band formed in December 1988 when Alex James joined Damon Albarn's band Circus, which renamed itself Seymour after J. D. Salinger's Seymour: An Introduction.
They played their first gig, as Seymour, in summer 1989 in the goods shed of the East Anglian Railway Museum at Chappel & Wakes Colne.
In 1995's “Battle of Britpop”, they had their first number one when ‘Country House’ outsold Oasis's ‘Roll with It’ by 274,000 copies to 216,000.

3hyGGjxu73JuzBa757H6R5.name: The Mountain Goats
f: For Rian Johnson, the band recorded ‘The Ultimate Jedi Who Wastes All the Other Jedi and Eats Their Bones’, a joke alternate plot for Star Wars: The Last Jedi.
Their name is a reference to Screamin' Jay Hawkins's song ‘Yellow Coat’, and for many years John Darnielle was the band's only member.
Unable to tour in March 2020, John Darnielle got out his old Panasonic boombox and recorded the band's first direct-to-boombox songs since 2002.
John Darnielle published his first novel, Wolf in White Van, on 16 September 2014; two days later it was nominated for the National Book Award for Fiction.
John Darnielle worked as a psychiatric nurse at the Metropolitan State Hospital in Norwalk, California.

3mY9Ii0cL5SQxpOTAm8SHx.name: Warren Zevon
f: By the age of 13, he was an occasional visitor to Igor Stravinsky's home, where he briefly studied modern classical music alongside Robert Craft.
He quit high school and drove a sports car his father had won in a card game from Los Angeles to New York, to become a folk singer.
In summer 1975 he briefly moved to Spain, playing the Dubliner Bar in Sitges; with its mercenary owner, David Lindell, he wrote ‘Roland the Headless Thompson Gunner’.
Back in Los Angeles by September 1975, he roomed with Fleetwood Mac's Stevie Nicks and Lindsey Buckingham.
When Asylum Records dropped him after The Envoy, he found out only by reading about it in Rolling Stone's “Random Notes” column.

3wrtQM9ICPPeHwoc1GWiyV.name: Teleman
f: Teleman's name was inspired by an album by the composer Georg Philipp Telemann that the band found in a charity shop.
Pete Cattermoul and brothers Jonny and Thomas Sanders started the band in 2011, after their previous band, Pete and the Pirates, broke up.
BBC 6 Music's Marc Riley championed the band, booking them for a session on his show in January 2013 and two more in 2014.
Keyboard player Jonny Sanders left the band in September 2020 and now makes music and lyric videos as Prehuman, including some for them.

3DL71JYSG6VREkmLSzfWhU.name: Efterklang
f: Their fourth album shares its name with its setting: Piramida, an abandoned mining town deep within the Arctic Circle.
In August 2010, the band and French filmmaker Vincent Moon met on an island off the Danish coast to shoot An Island, a film the length of an album.
They toured Piramida in 2012 with an orchestra and Siouxsie and the Banshees drummer Budgie, premiering it at the Sydney Opera House.
The name Efterklang comes from the Danish word for “remembrance” or “reverberation”.
They run their own label, Rumraket – Danish for “space rocket” – which has released records by Grizzly Bear and Amiina.

1i8jM74ElAevHmCU1sbNJM.name: Dean & Britta
f: After Luna split in 2005, they spent a year on film scores, most notably for Noah Baumbach's The Squid and the Whale.
Dean Wareham and Britta Phillips married during the recording of their album Back Numbers, and shortened the duo's name to Dean & Britta.
Dean Wareham formed Luna in 1991 after leaving Galaxie 500; Britta Phillips joined Luna in 2000, replacing bassist Justin Harwood.
In 2008, they covered The Cure's ‘Friday I'm in Love’ for the tribute album Just Like Heaven.

6v0kvTi9pOI2ZFrWGQhdsc.name: Apollo 100
f: Tom Parker formed the band in late 1971 with session musicians including drummer Clem Cattini, guitarists Vic Flick and Zed Jenkins, and bassist Brian Odgers.
Their follow-up to ‘Joy’, ‘Mendelssohn's 4th (Second Movement)’, reached only number 94 in the US in 1972, and the group broke up in 1973.
Their 1979 album Reach for the Sky reached number 37 in Australia.

7pZFNZpqGlLKcQcN0GCmdP.name: Tom Parker
f: He arranged the US Top 20 hit ‘Chirpy Chirpy Cheep Cheep’ and a number of Don Fardon's recordings.
He played keyboards, clarinet, saxophone, trumpet and trombone from an early age, and was working as a session musician by the 1960s.
He worked with groups including The Mark Leeman 5, Jimmy James and the Vagabonds, and Eric Burdon with the New Animals.
After Apollo 100, he went on to form the New London Chorale.

6CD0HbcaKmuVB3NHJJgSdH.name: Deep Sea Diver
f: After a big label deal at 19 didn't work out, the group's Jessica Dobson became a touring musician, first in Beck's band and then with the Shins.
On 10 July 2023 they were announced as support for fellow Seattle band Pearl Jam on several dates of its autumn 2023 North American tour.
In 2009 Jessica Dobson recorded and released an EP, New Caves, under the name Deep Sea Diver, with her husband, the drummer Peter Mansen.
They self-released their first two albums, History Speaks (2012) and Secrets (2016), and signed with Sub Pop in September 2024.

2wJ4vsxWd7df7dRU4KcoDe.name: Sharon Van Etten
f: In April 2020 she played bass and sang harmonies with the three surviving members of Fountains of Wayne, filling Adam Schlesinger's place at a televised benefit.
She scored the 2016 film Strange Weather in a practice space she shared with Michael Cera, recording dozens of demos for new songs in between.
She played Rachel in both series of Netflix's The OA, and performed ‘Tarifa’ in episode six of Showtime's 2017 Twin Peaks series.
Before her studio debut, she worked at Astor Wines and as a publicist at Ba Da Bing Records, which released her second album, Epic, in 2010.
She and Angel Olsen wore similar shag haircuts in the video for their 2021 single ‘Like I Used To’, produced by John Congleton.

0OnPrsDBROxkpC3qbFnL6L.name: FFS
f: The band exists because Alex Kapranos cracked a tooth on tour in Uruguay in 2013; looking for Huey Lewis's dentist in San Francisco, he bumped into Ron and Russell Mael.
Sparks opened the collaboration by sending Franz Ferdinand a song called ‘Collaborations Don't Work’; the bands then worked in secret for 18 months, swapping tracks.
Franz Ferdinand and Sparks first swapped demos in 2004; one, ‘Piss Off’, became the twelfth track on FFS, and Sparks' demo came out on a 2019 hits album.
FFS, short for Franz Ferdinand and Sparks, was announced as a supergroup on 9 March 2015.
The supergroup was Nick McCarthy's last project alongside the members of Franz Ferdinand before he left that band.
Five former members of the band went on to run five different recording studios in five different cities, including Austin, Nashville and Tulsa.
Robert Christgau said their 1979 debut would be remembered as a classic once CBS broke a few hits from it, then added: “But CBS won't.”
After Look Out!, the band's Steve Allen and Ron Flynt decided they were too good for Portrait, turned down a contract extension and left the label.
The band's Steve Allen moved from Tulsa to Los Angeles in 1977 after fellow Tulsa natives Phil Seymour and Dwight Twilley met with success.
The idea and the name for 20/20 came from Mike Gallo, who had dreamed them up after spending time in the UK, before he met Steve Allen in Los Angeles.

3zunDAtRDg7kflREzWAhxl.name: Eels
f: Eels were named so their records would sit alphabetically near Mark Oliver Everett's solo albums as E, but Eagles and Earth, Wind and Fire releases ended up in between.
In 2013 they released a parody video, ‘Cold Dead Hand’, through Funny or Die, with Jim Carrey replacing Mark Oliver Everett on vocals.
Their ‘Fresh Blood’ became the theme song of the 2015 HBO documentary series The Jinx.
They were one of the first acts to sign to DreamWorks Records, followed by Elliott Smith.
They won Best International Breakthrough Act at the 1998 BRIT Awards.

6XtG9W2KkPiQ6n1rlIvTJE.name: Robert Ellis
f: Billy Joel and Elton John may seem obvious touchstones for Texas Piano Man, but he says he drew his inspiration from a more unlikely source: Liberace.
He learned piano before he ever picked up a guitar, and returned to it for Texas Piano Man because guitar had become “not fresh” for him.
He sold his self-released LP The Great Rearranger at shows; then American Songwriter named his second album, Photographs, one of the top 50 albums of 2011.
In 2012 he moved from Austin to Nashville to make his third album, The Lights from the Chemical Plant, with producer Jacquire King.
He started out performing as “Eyes Like Lions” in 2005 in his hometown of Lake Jackson, Texas.

7guDJrEfX3qb6FEbdPA5qi.name: Stevie Wonder
f: He was 13 when the live ‘Fingertips’ topped the Hot 100; on it, a replacement bass player caught out by his spontaneous encore calls out “What key?”
In 1968 he recorded an album of mostly harmonica instrumentals titled Eivets Rednow – his name spelled backwards.
Because of his age, Motown held his royalties in trust until he was 21 and paid him $2.50 a week.
At 11, he sang his own song ‘Lonely Boy’ to Ronnie White of the Miracles, who took him to audition at Motown, where Berry Gordy signed him.
He wrote songs for Motown labelmates, including ‘The Tears of a Clown’, whose 1970 success as a single made Smokey Robinson reconsider leaving the Miracles.

7bhMBjjQhgPX0q9S4Ajncn.name: Ben Kweller
f: He learned ‘Heart and Soul’ on piano at eight, and by nine had a dozen songs and an honourable mention in a Billboard songwriting contest.
Nils Lofgren, who grew up with Ben Kweller's father, recommended Kweller's band Radish to producer Roger Greenawalt; a bidding war followed and Radish signed to Mercury.
He co-wrote Guster's ‘I Hope Tomorrow Is Like Today’ after a late-night jam and sang lead on it; the song features prominently in Wedding Crashers.
His self-released EP Freak Out, It's Ben Kweller caught the attention of the Lemonheads' Evan Dando, who took him on tour.
In 2003 he toured Australia with Ben Folds and Ben Lee as The Bens, making a four-song EP with each Ben singing lead on one song.

5PPCkoOKabpGGhqrUwSikz.name: Kimya Dawson
