f: She once joked that she was a cousin of the Strokes' drummer Fabrizio Moretti, and the joke grew into a myth that they really are cousins.
Her friend the wrestler Bryan Danielson (Daniel Bryan) guests on ‘Captain Lou’, her Thunder Thighs homage to wrestling manager Lou Albano.
She co-founded the Moldy Peaches with Adam Green; their ‘Anyone Else but You’, sung by Michael Cera and Elliot Page, charted on the Hot 100 after Juno.
The Juno soundtrack, with five of her solo songs, reached number one on the Billboard 200 in its third week in shops and won a Grammy in 2009.
She and Aesop Rock record as the Uncluded; the video for their single ‘Delicate Cycle’ includes a cameo from Lil Bub.

3oAbjWINfcTSAuVUlXXMty.name: Steve Forbert
f: He has a cameo as Cyndi Lauper's boyfriend in her ‘Girls Just Want to Have Fun’ video.
Hailed by the Village Voice as “the new Dylan”, he said he was “off the hook” because he didn't have to “know all the answers like Bob Dylan”.
After junior college and a spell as a truck driver, he moved to New York in 1976, busking in Greenwich Village and playing early shows at CBGB.
In September 2011 a Nashville gallery opened an exhibition of photographs he took with an old LG phone.
Any Old Time, his tribute album to Jimmie Rodgers, was nominated for a 2004 Grammy in the Best Traditional Folk category.

4OTD2AbOu5iBqSWk3NfwG5.name: Getdown Services
f: They self-released their 2022 single ‘Biscuit Tin’ with the proceeds going to the local chapter of the ACORN renters' union.
In 2026 they played London's Southbank Centre as part of the Meltdown festival curated by Harry Styles.
They have a cult following and a reputation as “Britain's best band”, and sold out a UK headline tour in autumn 2024.
Ben Sadler and Josh Law met at school in Minehead, Somerset; they signed with Bristol-based Breakfast Records and released their debut album, Crisps.
They describe their sound as “disco and eighties and like seventies infused groove based music”.

5wjWLK4KMqmRbdUtTEV1BG.name: Har Mar Superstar
f: Sean Tillmann named Har Mar Superstar after the Har Mar Mall in Roseville, Minnesota, but at first claimed Har Mar was his twin brother, ‘Harold Martin Tillmann’.
He first toured in a choir robe, backed only by pre-recorded beats played from his MiniDisc player.
After Britney Spears's management rejected his song ‘Tall Boy’, he recorded it himself for his album Dark Touches.
He plays Dancing Rick, a disco dance champion who takes on Ben Stiller's character, in the 2004 film Starsky & Hutch.
Minneapolis mayor R. T. Rybak declared 20 September 2013 ‘Har Mar Superstar Day’.

13jvSWmroZLlHV9cJqB5g4.name: Bobby Conn
f: He promoted himself as a potential Antichrist, figuring nobody would take it seriously because it was ‘about the dumbest thing you could say’.
On his 1998 album Rise Up!, he promised the end of the world on his 33rd birthday.
At high school he started a hardcore punk trio, The Broken Kockamamies, whose only prop was a set of eight-foot strobe lights called ‘the pillars of fear’.
He said two songs on his 2007 album King for a Day were about Tom Cruise, adding that he didn't know a more political statement.
In 2003 he produced a session for the Cribs, who had supported him on a UK tour; part of it appeared on their 2004 debut.

6yjU0SoX3vxPV7KoopXlWe.name: Carole Bayer Sager
f: She wrote her first pop hit, ‘A Groovy Kind of Love’, with Toni Wine while still a student at New York's High School of Music and Art.
She contributed lyrics to ‘Ghost Town’ on Kanye West's album Ye.
She wrote the lyrics to ‘Nobody Does It Better’, the Bond theme Carly Simon sang in The Spy Who Loved Me (1977), to Marvin Hamlisch's music.
She and Burt Bacharach wrote ‘That's What Friends Are For’ for the 1982 film Night Shift; it won the 1987 Grammy for Song of the Year.
She won the 1982 Academy Award for Best Original Song for ‘Arthur's Theme (Best That You Can Do)’.

1NpeO0rYdDwUjtaXMDlb25.name: Rob Moose
f: He left a master's programme in American studies at Columbia University to tour with Antony and the Johnsons in 2005.
Playing violin, viola, guitar and mandolin, he has performed on close to 500 albums.
He has written arrangements for records by Taylor Swift, Paul Simon, Phoebe Bridgers and They Might Be Giants.
He has songwriting credits on Bon Iver's ‘iMi’, ‘Holyfields’ and ‘Marion’, and conducted the band's ‘Worm Crew’ on their 2019 album I, I.
From 2019 to 2020 he analysed popular songs for the Headgum podcast Punch Up the Jam.

4XquDVA8pkg5Lx91No1JxB.name: Brittany Howard
f: She grew up in a family home in a junk yard, which once burned down after a lightning strike.
At Lollapalooza in 2015, she was invited on stage to sing ‘Get Back’ as a duet with Paul McCartney.
The actor Terry Crews lip-syncs her vocal in the video for her 2019 single ‘Stay High’.
After high school she worked for the United States Postal Service until she became lead singer of Alabama Shakes full-time.
She and Ludwig Göransson co-wrote ‘Pale Pale Moon’, featured in Ryan Coogler's film Sinners; the soundtrack has both her demo and Jayme Lawson's film version.

1ZzqxDkqNDAJVaNO1xue3P.name: Fabiana Palladino
f: Jai Paul found her on SoundCloud while she was working in the Old Vic box office, and signed her to his label, the Paul Institute.
Despite a ‘richly musical household’ as the daughter of Welsh musician Pino Palladino, she did not intend to make music professionally.
In 2023 she and her brother Rocco Palladino played in Jai Paul's band at his Coachella debut.
Through Myspace she met Sampha, who later produced her 2014 single ‘For You’.
She worked as audio engineer on ‘Current Affairs’ and ‘If She Could See Me Now’ from Lorde's fourth studio album, Virgin.

37uLId6Z5ZXCx19vuruvv5.name: Hot Chip
f: The band's Alexis Taylor says a Royal Trux concert he attended with Joe Goddard was the moment that ‘changed it all’ for him.
Their ‘Ready for the Floor’ was nominated for the Grammy for Best Dance Recording but lost to Daft Punk's ‘Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger (Alive 2007)’.
In 2008 Robert Wyatt sang reworked versions of three tracks from their Made in the Dark for an EP with the band.
They produced official remixes for Kraftwerk in 2007.
The band's Joe Goddard released a solo track, ‘Gabriel’, that featured in the 2013 video game Grand Theft Auto V.

4x1nvY2FN8jxqAFA0DA02H.name: John Lennon
f: He called the eleven-plus ‘the only exam I ever passed, because I was terrified’.
His mother, Julia Lennon, lent him five pounds and ten shillings for his first guitar, on condition it was delivered to her house rather than his aunt's.
His first song, ‘Hello Little Girl’, became a UK top 10 hit for the Fourmost in 1963.
His middle name, Winston, came from the Prime Minister Winston Churchill.
In the mid-1960s he published In His Own Write and A Spaniard in the Works, collections of nonsense writing and line drawings.

6Lll1MPPak4m4vZKuJB264.name: BRONCHO
f: Their ‘It's On’ played over the closing credits of ‘Females Only’, the first episode of the third season of HBO's Girls.
Their ‘Try Me Out Sometime’ was used in an HBO Now advert, the film Movie 43 and the documentary Valley Uprising.
Their ‘Boys Got to Go’ was on the soundtrack of the 2019 football video game PES 2020.
The band formed in Norman, Oklahoma, in 2010; their debut album, Can't Get Past the Lips, came out in 2011 and was re-released in 2013.

4DLjEphXbW7qIhX4iwmNEe.name: Fat Dog
f: The band's former drummer Johnny Hutch got the nickname ‘Doghead’ from playing every gig with a latex dog mask on his head.
Formed during the COVID-19 lockdowns, they were called ‘2023's wildest live band’ by NME's Gary Ryan before they had released a single.
Their first single, ‘King of the Slugs’ (2023), was a seven-minute punk-and-techno track co-produced by frontman Joe Love and James Ford.
Their frontman Joe Love has cited the music from Serious Sam as an influence on the band's mix of dance, punk and klezmer.
They have opened for Viagra Boys and Yard Act, and sold out Scala on their debut headline tour.

594LqcHtMvKoR0URmSiYJB.name: Syreeta
f: When Diana Ross left the Supremes in 1970, Berry Gordy considered replacing her with Syreeta Wright, but offered the place to Jean Terrell.
Brian Holland found ‘Syreeta’ hard to pronounce, so her first solo single, in January 1968, came out under the name Rita Wright.
She sang the demo vocals for the Supremes' hit ‘Love Child’.
She co-wrote Stevie Wonder's hit ‘Signed, Sealed, Delivered (I'm Yours)’ and sang backing vocals on it.
In the mid-1970s she lived briefly in Ethiopia, working as a Transcendental Meditation teacher.

3fhOTtm0LBJ3Ojn4hIljLo.name: Roxy Music
f: Bryan Ferry picked the name Roxy from a list of old cinemas for its ‘faded glamour’, adding ‘Music’ after learning of an American band called Roxy.
Island Records boss Chris Blackwell seemed unimpressed by the band until he glanced at their debut album's cover and asked, ‘Have we got them signed yet?’
Phil Manzanera missed out at his first audition for the band and became their roadie; when the guitar job reopened, he had secretly learned their entire repertoire.
Andy Mackay answered Bryan Ferry's November 1970 advert for a keyboardist; Ferry had just lost his job teaching ceramics at a girls' school for holding record-listening sessions.
Robert Fripp and Peter Sinfield judged Bryan Ferry's voice wrong for King Crimson but were impressed enough to help Roxy Music get a deal with E.G. Records.

5EOPLr73C9nIPYwVEAsiOY.name: Ed Harcourt
f: He worked as a beekeeper and a chef before starting his first band.
He reached grade 8 piano at 17 but turned down the chance to study music, saying dissecting it ‘would completely destroy any enjoyment’.
In 2000 he recorded his debut mini-album, Maplewood EP, straight to a 4-track recorder at Wootton Manor.
He played piano with the Libertines when they were the surprise guests on Glastonbury's Pyramid stage on 26 June 2015.
On 22 October 2017 he led a band playing the whole of Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band live at the Philharmonie de Paris.

1gxczmVzWKNJLz61uI27zJ.name: Evangeline
f: She found a sold-out launch show for her debut album, in an LA record shop holding about 100 people, far more nerve-racking than Madison Square Garden.
In college she gigged with a band and released songs as Eva B. Ross, leading to collaborations with Big Thief's Buck Meek and Christian Lee Hutson.
Her first supporting role as an actor was in Winter Spring Summer or Fall, a Paramount film starring Jenna Ortega.
She first wrote ‘You and Me’ nearly five years before its 2024 release, reviving it in a jam with producer Max Shrager while listening to a lot of JJ Cale.
When she was about ten, her father asked her and her sisters to try writing songs for the family band.

7fIfKG7oJGO4p8wvyi6adh.name: E.U.
f: Beck sampled their ‘Knock Him Out Sugar Ray’ just before the second verse of his hit ‘Where It's At’.
Producer Marvin Ennis played every instrument and sang all the backing vocals on ‘Taste of Your Love’, their last Billboard top-ten hit, whatever the album credits say.
E.U. stands for Experience Unlimited, a Washington, D.C. go-go and funk band fronted by singer and bassist Gregory ‘Sugar Bear’ Elliot.
Public Enemy sampled the band's ‘E.U. Freeze’ on their single ‘Night of the Living Baseheads’.
In 2023 their ‘Hey You’, from their 1977 debut album, was used in New Balance advertisements.

1SQRv42e4PjEYfPhS0Tk9E.name: The Kinks
f: Dave Davies got the distorted guitar on the band's ‘You Really Got Me’ by slicing the speaker cone of his Elpico amplifier, the ‘little green amp’.
When Pye refused to pay for a remake of the band's ‘You Really Got Me’, managers Grenville Collins and Robert Wace funded it themselves; it went to number one.
Rod Stewart, a fellow pupil at William Grimshaw school, sang with the band that became the Kinks at least once in early 1962.
Problems on their 1965 American tour got the band banned from touring the US for several years.
Ray Davies recalled that manager Larry Page named the Kinks after their ‘kinky’ fashion sense; Davies has said, ‘I've never really liked the name’.

2i1IdHG5w0wiSmJGoqAGlj.name: Minnie Riperton
f: The melody of her ‘Lovin' You’ was created to distract her baby daughter, the future comedian Maya Rudolph, so Minnie Riperton and Richard Rudolph could spend time together.
She had operatic training as a girl at Chicago's Abraham Lincoln Center, and became known for her five-octave range and use of the whistle register.
In 1973 a college intern for Epic Records found her in semi-retirement, a homemaker and mother of two in Gainesville, Florida.
She released her first local hit, ‘Lonely Girl’, as Andrea Davis, in honour of its writer, her mentor Billy Davis.
Her girl group the Gems, working as the session group Studio Three, sang backing vocals on Fontella Bass's 1965 hit ‘Rescue Me’.

4vjGlQWexbru6aOUCLTVir.name: Kiki Dee
f: She was the first female singer from the UK to sign with Motown's Tamla Records.
Songwriter Mitch Murray turned Pauline Matthews into Kiki Dee, creating her stage name and writing her first single, ‘Early Night’.
She sang backing vocals on Love Affair's ‘Everlasting Love’, a UK number one in 1968.
Her 1976 duet with Elton John, ‘Don't Go Breaking My Heart’, reached number one in the UK and the US, and held the UK top spot for six weeks.
At the end of summer 1976 she was the support act for Queen's Hyde Park concert, in front of a crowd of 150,000.

20vuBdFblWUo2FCOvUzusB.name: David Byrne
f: He was rejected from his middle school choir for being ‘off-key and too withdrawn’.
Born in Dumbarton, Scotland, he grew up speaking with a Scottish accent but adopted an American one to fit in at school.
He shared an Academy Award for Best Original Score with Ryuichi Sakamoto and Cong Su for Bernardo Bertolucci's The Last Emperor (1987).
He and Brian Eno made My Life in the Bush of Ghosts between 1979 and 1981, an album acclaimed for its early use of sampling and found sounds.
He and Fatboy Slim made Here Lies Love, a disco opera about the life of Imelda Marcos, former First Lady of the Philippines.

5lkiCO9UQ8B23dZ1o0UV4m.name: Jackson Browne
f: At his 2004 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction, Bruce Springsteen told him the Eagles got in first, but ‘You wrote the songs they wished they had written.’
In 2008 he sued John McCain and the Republican Party for using ‘Running on Empty’ in an ad; the 2009 settlement came with an apology.
He recorded Running on Empty (1977) entirely on tour, mixing new songs played live with recordings made on buses, in hotel rooms and backstage.
At the age of three he moved into Abbey San Encino in Los Angeles, built by his grandfather Clyde Browne.
Before he turned 18, he was a staff writer in Greenwich Village for Elektra's publishing company, Nina Music.

1yap1SgRPMxgyfrrDlQ95y.name: Emitt Rhodes
f: Some listeners speculated that his 1970 album was a secret Beatles or Paul McCartney record; his Beatles-like style earned him the nickname ‘one-man Beatles’.
He recorded his self-titled 1970 album in his parents' garage, which he had converted into a studio, playing every instrument himself.
His ABC/Dunhill contract demanded an album every six months for three years; by December 1971 the label had sued him for $250,000.
His Troubadour debut in February 1971 coincided with the San Fernando earthquake; Billboard joked, ‘That wasn't an earthquake, that was Emitt Rhodes opening at the Troubadour!’
He began working with producer Chris Price in 2014; the result, Rainbow Ends (2016), was his first album in 43 years.

22bE4uQ6baNwSHPVcDxLCe.name: The Rolling Stones
f: Mick Jagger and Keith Richards met again at Dartford railway station on 17 October 1961, when Jagger was carrying Chuck Berry and Muddy Waters records.
According to Keith Richards, Brian Jones named the band during a call to Jazz News, after spotting the track ‘Rollin' Stone’ on a Muddy Waters LP on the floor.
Andrew Loog Oldham was 19 when he became their manager in 1963, younger than anyone in the band, and needed his mother to co-sign contracts.
Andrew Loog Oldham dropped keyboardist Ian Stewart from the band's official line-up, saying he didn't look the part and six faces were too many for fans to remember.
Bill Wyman auditioned for them in a Chelsea pub on 7 December 1962; the band were impressed by his instrument and amplifiers, including a Vox AC30.

07Pw9XQo0hIwtKRrBwo0Rl.name: Brenda Fassie
f: For all her outrageous, controversial stage presence, her name Nokuzola means ‘quiet’, ‘calm’ or ‘peace’.
Her career began in the vocal group Joy, filling in for a member on maternity leave, before she fronted Brenda and the Big Dudes.
Her ‘Black President’, about Nelson Mandela, was banned by the state as anti-apartheid, even though Mandela had been freed by the time it came out.
Time magazine dubbed her ‘The Madonna of the Townships’ in 2001.
Her mother was a pianist, and she was earning money singing for tourists by the age of five.

5eUda4BaWhUQWWJiP1ml5v.name: Sorry
f: Before writing their own songs, the band's Asha Lorenz and Louis O'Bryen posted several covers of Jimi Hendrix songs.
They call their music pop; Louis O'Bryen has said it is ‘a bit annoying to be called post-punk or grunge because I don't think we are that’.
They started out in 2014 under the name Fish, and became Sorry in 2016.
In February 2021 they announced a live album recorded at the Windmill, Brixton, with proceeds going to the venue, which was struggling after the pandemic.
Asha Lorenz and Louis O'Bryen write most of the songs as a duo; Lincoln Barrett, Campbell Baum and Marco Pini complete the band live.

3f626JSVauIhTQgatsFcs4.name: Paul Williams
f: He tried out for The Mickey Mouse Club in early 1955 and was turned down; in October 1980 he hosted its 25th anniversary special on NBC.
On 9 February 1973 he sang on The Tonight Show in full make-up as Virgil, the genius orangutan he played in Battle for the Planet of the Apes.
He wrote the lyrics and Barbra Streisand the melody of ‘Evergreen’, which won the Oscar for Best Original Song and the Grammy for Song of the Year.
‘We've Only Just Begun’, the Carpenters hit he wrote with Roger Nichols, began as a song for a Crocker National Bank TV commercial featuring newlyweds.
He co-wrote and sang ‘Touch’ on Daft Punk's Random Access Memories, and spoke for the duo when it won Album of the Year at the 2014 Grammys.

6jlWj6y00bMQt8XoKuCjyZ.name: Emily King
f: Her parents, Marion Cowings and Kim Kalesti, were a singing duo who toured regularly and took her and her older brother with them.
She signed her first record deal in 2004 and appeared that year on Nas's album Street's Disciple, credited simply as ‘Emily’.
She helped compose and sang ‘Being Human’, the end theme of Cartoon Network's Steven Universe Future.
Around the time of her album Scenery, she left New York City to try country living, and learned to drive and to feed a wood stove.
On 21 March 2021 she became Marc Rebillet's first ever guest performer on his live stream.

4wBhllC5Nto10UefzXVMt9.name: Omni
f: Vice's Drew Schwartz called them ‘the best post-punk band in America’.
They have said the lyrics and melodies of their song ‘Exacto’ were written in the back of a van in Sacramento.
Before Omni, Frankie Broyles played in Deerhunter and Balkans, Chris Yonker in Greenscreen and Philip Frobos in Carnivores.
Their sound draws on post-punk bands such as Television, Talking Heads and Wire, with ‘mathematical’ rhythms.

5TjpsMnYz8lxTr91olqbEh.name: P.P. Arnold
f: She once held two jobs to support her family: clerk-typist at a clothing firm by day, separating egg whites from yolks in an egg factory in the evenings.
She quit the Ike & Tina Turner Revue in autumn 1966, after its UK tour with the Rolling Stones, staying in London to go solo with Mick Jagger's encouragement.
She sang backing vocals on two of the Small Faces' biggest hits, ‘Itchycoo Park’ and ‘Tin Soldier’.
Her backing vocals feature prominently on Peter Gabriel's 1986 worldwide hit ‘Sledgehammer’.
A solo album Barry Gibb produced for her was never completed; she could only release the recordings in 2017, on The Turning Tide.

62sC6lUEWRjbFqXpMmOk4G.name: Fugazi
f: Ian MacKaye took the name Fugazi, meaning false or inauthentic, from Mark Baker's Nam, a collection of Vietnam War veterans' stories.
Atlantic Records president Ahmet Ertegun offered them ‘anything you want’, their own label and more than $10 million just to sign; they declined.
Producer Ted Niceley had become a chef, so he reluctantly declined to produce their album Steady Diet of Nothing, and the band produced it themselves.
Ian MacKaye's original concept for the band was ‘MC5 plus reggae’.
Guy Picciotto dropped by one of their practices to see how his Rites of Spring bandmate Brendan Canty was getting on; he later admitted he secretly hoped to join.

7K48RaFMB6BhTLc0KspbTh.name: Daryl Johns
f: Born to jazz musician parents, he was hailed by many in his earlier years as the foremost jazz upright bassist of his generation.
He left his home in New Jersey and moved to California to join Mac DeMarco's live band.
He has performed and recorded with Pat Metheny, Vijay Iyer, Immanuel Wilkins, the Lemon Twigs and Macy Gray.
Of his self-titled debut album, he said: ‘I just made it cuz I like it. I just wanna have fun.’

4CxobvwTpmfpIEbkYh4pAb.name: Eric Johnson
f: After a faulty part was replaced in his favourite Dumble amplifier, it never sounded the same, and he sold it to Carlos Santana.
His violin-like lead sound came from his beloved 1954 Fender Stratocaster, which he named Virginia.
An admitted perfectionist, he mastered and then scrapped several finished tracks for his follow-up to Ah Via Musicom, delaying it by three years.
He recorded his debut album, Seven Worlds, in Austin in 1976–78, but contract disputes kept it unreleased until 1998.
Unable to get a new management contract, he worked as a session guitarist for Cat Stevens, Carole King and Christopher Cross.

3sFhA6G1N0gG1pszb6kk1m.name: Wings
f: The name Wings is said to have come to Paul McCartney as he prayed in hospital while Linda McCartney gave birth to their daughter Stella McCartney in 1971.
They made Band on the Run, their most successful album, as a trio at EMI's primitive eight-track studio in Lagos, Nigeria.
On the first tour by an ex-Beatle after the split, they played no Beatles songs, to show they were a new band in their own right.
The BBC banned their ‘Give Ireland Back to the Irish’, yet it reached number 1 in the Republic of Ireland and Spain.
They went through three lead guitarists and four drummers, while the core trio of Paul and Linda McCartney and Denny Laine stayed throughout.

2Jv5eshHtLycR6R8KQCdc4.name: Grizzly Bear
f: The name Grizzly Bear began as Ed Droste's label for a solo home project, and was a nickname for an old boyfriend of his.
On the band's last date opening for Radiohead in 2008, in Toronto, Jonny Greenwood called them his favourite band from the stage.
They named their 2009 album Veckatimest after a tiny, uninhabited island on Cape Cod that the band visited.
Their album Yellow House was named after Ed Droste's mother's house, where it was recorded.
In 2020 Ed Droste confirmed he had left the band and enrolled in school to become a therapist; in 2025 they announced a tour with all four members.

4nymPwNq7Y6i1tVs1d9WVB.name: The Free Design
f: In 2000 they regrouped after nearly 30 years to record ‘Endless Harmony’ for a Beach Boys tribute album.
Stereolab named a 1999 single ‘The Free Design’, though the song had no direct connection to the band.
In 1994 the Japanese musician Cornelius reissued their catalogue on his Trattoria label.
The band's Chris Dedrick later moved to Toronto and won a Genie Award for Guy Maddin's film The Saddest Music in the World.
Their original line-up was three siblings: Chris, Sandy and Bruce Dedrick.

2wAPeWKKHrPZ3UUqnw9Bpy.name: Connie Converse
f: By the time her letters to her family were delivered, she had packed her belongings into her Volkswagen Beetle and driven away, never to be heard from again.
Her 1950s songs are among the earliest known recordings in the US singer-songwriter genre.
Her only known public performance was a brief 1954 appearance on CBS's The Morning Show with Walter Cronkite.
Biographer Howard Fishman writes that she lost her job when her institute landed in the cross hairs of the House Un-American Activities Committee.
About ten years after she disappeared, her family hired a private investigator, who told them it was her right to disappear.

18RkLKfeoUgZflWv9os25W.name: Miriam Makeba
f: Her first name, Zenzile, comes from a Xhosa word meaning ‘you brought this on yourself’, which her grandmother muttered to her mother after the birth.
At her New York debut, at the Village Vanguard, she sang in Xhosa and Zulu and a Yiddish folk song, with Miles Davis and Duke Ellington watching.
‘Lovely Lies’, her first recording in English, was the first South African record to chart on the US Billboard Top 100.
She made her US debut on The Steve Allen Show on 1 November 1959, before a television audience of 60 million.
She said she learned to sing in English before she could speak the language.

4Ajgo7nAsTzjSFymIfBjZ1.name: The Felice Brothers
f: When storms cut the power at the 2008 Newport Folk Festival, their stage had no generator, so they played unplugged.
From Palenville in the Catskills, they started out playing in New York's 42nd Street and Union Square subway stations.
Dell's 2013 advert ‘Beginnings’ used their cover of The Drifters' hit ‘This Magic Moment’.
Their ‘Radio Song’ plays on the bar jukebox in the 2017 film Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri.
A 2026 tribute album to the band, Felice County Fair, has covers by Bright Eyes, Phoebe Bridgers, The Lumineers and Old Crow Medicine Show.

1HkQ4XrPffqcVW0TgTTw0d.name: Yma Sumac
f: For years a rumour claimed Yma Sumac was a Brooklyn housewife called Amy Camus, who had reversed her name.
A December 1950 review by jazz critic Leonard Feather suggested her recorded voice was really a theremin, and that ‘Xtabay’ was Pig Latin for ‘Baxter’.
In 1946 the government of Peru formally supported her claim to be descended from Atahualpa, the last Inca emperor.
In 1956 she won a Guinness World Record for the Greatest Range of Musical Value.
Born Zoila Emperatriz Chávarri Castillo, she took her stage name from the Quechua ‘Ima sumaq’, meaning ‘how beautiful’.

7sECLFfpeGHQYRH7Lvc9pA.name: Arthur Lee
f: He said that for a recording of his song ‘My Diary’ he wanted a guitarist with a Curtis Mayfield–like feel, and label owner Billy Revis recommended Jimi Hendrix.
Love's 1969 album Four Sail, his pun on his original title For Sale, was ten songs Elektra founder Jac Holzman chose to fulfil Lee's contract.
Burt Bacharach gave a thumbs-down to Love's cover of ‘My Little Red Book’, which he wrote with Hal David: Arthur Lee's band had altered its chord changes.
His band Love recorded Forever Changes in only 64 hours, with session players standing in for band members on one or two songs.
In 1965 his folk rock group the Grass Roots renamed itself Love, because another signed act was already called the Grass Roots.

1bAdBYcsDdsbqmWbAE7qKR.name: JJ
f: JJ stands for “Joakim och jag”, Swedish for “Joakim and I”: the duo is Joakim Benon and Elin Kastlander.
They began so anonymously that only their label, Sincerely Yours, let on that the act was more than one person.
They gave away covers of Akon's ‘Troublemaker’, Jeremih's ‘Birthday Sex’ and the theme song from the TV series Welcome Back, Kotter.
Their song ‘My Life’ was used in an official trailer for the video game Battlefield 3 in April 2011.
In 2011 they released ‘We Can't Stop’ with Ne-Yo as part of Adult Swim's Singles Program.

4bthk9UfsYUYdcFyqxmSUU.name: Tears For Fears
f: On the morning of Live Aid it was announced that the duo, billed to appear before they had even agreed to, had pulled out.
Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith first called the duo History of Headaches; Tears for Fears was inspired by Arthur Janov's primal therapy.
When Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith met primal therapy's Arthur Janov in the mid-1980s, he had gone “Hollywood” and wanted them to write him a musical.
On tour, Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith found Oleta Adams performing in a Kansas City hotel bar and invited her to collaborate on their next album.
Before Tears for Fears, Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith were in the mod revival band Graduate, whose 1980 single ‘Elvis Should Play Ska’ referred to Elvis Costello.

3C8RpaI3Go0yFF9whvKoED.name: The Avalanches
f: Robbie Chater estimated that the band's debut album, Since I Left You, was built from about 3,500 vinyl samples, including Madonna's ‘Holiday’.
They spent a large amount of time scoring the 2013 stage show King Kong, but only a 25-second track of theirs was used.
They worked on an animated musical film described as a “hip hop version of Yellow Submarine”, which lost its funding and was never completed.
In 2006 their label Modular declared they had “made the record of their lives”, after a joke email claiming it had rejected their album reached the press.
They took their name, at their fifth gig, from an American surf rock band whose only album was Ski Surfin' with the Avalanches (1963).

66uU7VPJQ8eC06LAZyqYYk.name: Dead Man's Bones
f: Ryan Gosling and Zach Shields met in 2005 and found they shared an obsession with Disneyland's Haunted Mansion ride.
Ryan Gosling and Zach Shields set out to write love stories about ghosts and monsters; Gosling's parents had left his childhood home believing it haunted.
On the band's album, Ryan Gosling and Zach Shields played every instrument, even ones they'd never touched, with no click track, trying for at most three takes a song.
Touring the US in autumn 2009, Ryan Gosling and Zach Shields played with a local children's choir and staged a talent show at every gig.
Their use of a children's choir was cited as inspiring blackened death metal band Behemoth to use one on their 2018 album I Loved You at Your Darkest.

6f1YthbbEpu9qHzOUW2UYI.name: Tonight
f: Their manager believed in the band so much that he sold his own property to finance them.
They and the Rich Kids were the first acts called power pop, a term Charles Catchpole first used in the Evening Standard on 17 January 1978.
They were told they needed another Top 20 hit before their album could come out; when their third single flopped, the indebted band split in January 1979.
Their album Drummerman was shelved by WEA in 1978 and finally released by Angel Air Records in 2010.

6CFQDzNLNcuK5lVZ766Yxt.name: Yannis
f: In 2018 he started MILK, a south London club night with secret guests; every night is recorded and sold on vinyl at the next month's event.
Yannis Philippakis formed Foals in 2005 after his band the Edmund Fitzgerald broke up; Foals drummer Jack Bevan had also been in the Edmund Fitzgerald.
He studied English literature at St John's College, Oxford, but dropped out before finishing his degree to focus on his band.
As Yannis & The Yaw, he made the 2024 EP Lagos Paris London with the late Nigerian musician Tony Allen.
His father, whom he visited each summer in Olympos on the Greek island of Karpathos, taught him traditional Greek songs.

3PP6ghmOlDl2jaKaH0avUN.name: Black Country, New Road
f: Isaac Wood named Black Country, New Road after a road in the West Midlands that he found using Wikipedia's random-article button.
Out of respect for former singer Isaac Wood, they don't play songs from their first two albums live, but are open to his return.
After their second single, ‘Sunglasses’ (2019), The Quietus's John Doran called them “the best in the entire world”.
Physical copies of their first two singles, ‘Athens, France’ and ‘Sunglasses’, were reportedly resold for over £100.
Their Never Again EP, limited to 1,500 copies, covered songs by MGMT, ABBA and Adele.

4T4JE09FOmRgv2Wzb6JaOR.name: Willie J Healey
f: He added the “J” because “Willie Healey” on its own “sounded like it needed something going on in the middle”.
He first planned to be a boxer and, before his record deal, worked with his dad as a plasterer in Carterton.
He says Jamie T lent him a drum machine during lockdown, which led to the more funk-based sound of his album Bunny.
He taught himself music from 13, wanting to play Oasis covers with his dad and grandad, who always played at Christmas.
He supported Florence & the Machine and Arctic Monkeys on their 2023 tours, and Idles on their 2024 UK tour.

0Mz5XE0kb1GBnbLQm2VbcO.name: Mos Def
f: Mos Def, short for “Most Definitely”, retired the name in 2011, announcing that he had legally become Yasiin Bey.
He made his acting debut while still at high school, in the 1988 film God Bless the Child starring Mare Winningham.
Around the time of Black on Both Sides (1999), he also contributed to the Scritti Politti album Anomie & Bonhomie.
In 2010 he featured alongside soul legend Bobby Womack on ‘Stylo’, the first single from Gorillaz's album Plastic Beach.
In 1996 he and fellow Brooklyn rapper Talib Kweli formed the duo Black Star.

1HOeqtP7tHkKNJNLzQ2tnr.name: Everything Everything
f: They took their name from the first two words of Radiohead's ‘Everything in Its Right Place’, the opening track of Kid A.
Their Get to Heaven lyrics were inspired when Jonathan Higgs started watching rolling news on a loop; reading them back, he realised he'd ‘written a horror bible’.
Before the band, Jonathan Higgs, on drums, and Jeremy Pritchard played in Salford math rock trio Modern Bison, whose only album was I Could Have Had a Rustic Pagoda.
NME hailed them as ‘pop's new Picassos’ for Man Alive, which was shortlisted for the 2011 Mercury Prize but lost to PJ Harvey's Let England Shake.
Founding guitarist Alex Niven left the band to pursue a career in academia; Alex Robertshaw, whose band Operahouse had split months earlier, replaced him.

4MGA6AM4iZ2HYc6b77og9g.name: Dirty Nice
f: The band's management agreed they could release ‘If I Was Abducted by Aliens’ if its teaser got 50,000 likes; it reached 93,000.
They pair Charlie Pelling, composer of the surreal Channel 4 show Don't Hug Me I'm Scared, with Lisbon-based musician Mark Thompson.
They started out hoping for Banksy- or Daft Punk-style anonymity, wearing digital masks instead of helmets, but revealed their identities in order to tour.
They played their first gig at a kid's birthday party, and later grew into a six-piece live band that played Maida Vale for BBC Introducing.
They released their debut album, Lobster, in 2021 and won a famous fan in Florence Pugh, who hailed them on the Vogue podcast.

4UvhuGdFf75Cfan7lEU1J1.name: The Books
f: In 2004 the French Ministry of Culture asked them to compose music for a new lift in its building.
The band's Nick Zammuto and Paul de Jong met as New York neighbours in 1999; over dinner, de Jong played Zammuto samples including a Shooby Taylor record.
They finished recording their debut, Thought for Food, in the basement of a North Carolina hostel where Nick Zammuto worked after hiking the Appalachian Trail.
Before a three-month North American tour in April 2006, they had played only one concert, at a Chicago festival in October 2003.
They rarely used a drum kit, instead sampling and looping everyday objects such as children's toys and filing cabinets.

5GGJosGMs08YEmKTZJe1fL.name: Suki Waterhouse
f: She asked Mick Fleetwood to drum on her song ‘Morals’, and received ‘a billion videos’ of him playing takes in a studio in Hawaii.
She played keyboardist Karen Sirko in Daisy Jones & the Six; showrunner Scott Neustadter made the novel's American character British.
She was discovered as a model at 16 in ‘either a Topshop or H&M’ in London.
Her single ‘Good Looking’, released between 2017 and 2019, became a viral hit in 2022.
In August 2024 she opened for Taylor Swift's Eras Tour at Wembley Stadium.

54KCNI7URCrG6yjQK3Ukow.name: Susanne Sundfør
f: Accepting the Spellemannprisen for Female Artist, she sparked nationwide debate by saying her work represented her as an artist first and a woman second.
She sang the main vocal on ‘Oblivion’, the title song of M83's soundtrack for the 2013 film Oblivion.
Her A Night at Salle Pleyel, commissioned for the Oslo Jazz Festival's 25th anniversary, is a live piece for synthesisers alone, played by four keyboardists she chose.
Her second album, The Brothel, was Norway's best-selling album of 2010; she said it was the first time she felt she had ‘found’ a sound.
She sang a Norwegian folk-tune psalm on Sorgen og Gleden, an album by Mette-Marit, Crown Princess of Norway.

5X3TuTi9OIsJXMGxPwTKM2.name: The Young Rascals
f: ‘The Rascals are coming!’ was posted on the Shea Stadium scoreboard at the Beatles' 1965 tour opener, until Beatles manager Brian Epstein had it removed.
Paul McCartney was so excited by their UK debut in London on 1 December 1966 that he went to their show the next night too.
They were the first all-white act signed by Atlantic Records, then mainly a label for black artists, on a $15,000 contract.
Manager Sid Bernstein renamed the band the Young Rascals after Borrah Minnevitch's Harmonica Rascals objected to them making records as the Rascals.
They were known for refusing to tour on segregated bills, and their final US number one, ‘People Got to Be Free’, was a plea for racial tolerance.

77tT1kLj6mCWtFNqiOmP9H.name: Daryl Hall & John Oates
f: Hall & Oates got their nickname from a shared apartment's mailbox, but all their US releases credit them by full name, Daryl Hall and John Oates.
Their ‘I Can't Go for That (No Can Do)’ is one of the few songs by a white act to top both the US R&B and pop charts.
Pierre LaRoche, creator of David Bowie's Ziggy Stardust cover, designed their 1975 silver album cover, showing them so made up they looked feminine.
They met at the Adelphi Ballroom in Philadelphia in 1967, each leading his own group: the Temptones and the Masters.
They remain the most successful duo of all time, ahead of the Carpenters, the Everly Brothers and Simon & Garfunkel.

32vWCbZh0xZ4o9gkz4PsEU.name: Dolly Parton
f: When Elvis Presley wanted to record ‘I Will Always Love You’, Colonel Tom Parker demanded half the publishing; she refused, a decision that later earned her millions.
Her father paid the missionary who delivered her, Robert F. Thomas, with a sack of cornmeal.
Monument Records first pitched her as a bubblegum pop singer and resisted her recording country, thinking her unusually high soprano unsuited to it.
At 13 she recorded ‘Puppy Love’ and appeared at the Grand Ole Opry, where Johnny Cash encouraged her to follow her own instincts.
She wrote more than 3,000 songs and had 44 top ten country albums, a record for any artist.

1667U2YoucgG5Pdvm2M59c.name: Orleans
f: Their label Infinity Records went bankrupt in 1980 after an album of performances by Pope John Paul II failed to sell.
Rolling Stone once called them ‘the best unrecorded band in America’.
Their ‘Still the One’ was chosen as the theme song of the ABC television network in January 1977.
The band's founder John Hall and his wife Johanna Hall wrote ‘Half Moon’, which appeared on Janis Joplin's posthumous album Pearl.
They took their name from the music they played when they formed, inspired partly by Louisiana artists such as Allen Toussaint and the Neville Brothers.

6hAUCkzZpoYGObd8qFW5TT.name: Pokey LaFarge
f: Born Andrew Heissler, he got his nickname from his mother, who used to scold him to hurry up when he was a child.
In the documentary The American Epic Sessions, his band recorded ‘St. Louis Blues’ on the first electrical sound recording system, from the 1920s.
At 17 he hitchhiked to the west coast and made his living busking on streets, sidewalks and pedestrian malls.
After hearing Bill Monroe at 16, he traded the guitar his grandfather had given him for a mandolin.
Jack White produced an album for Pokey LaFarge's band, then had them play on ‘I Guess I Should Go to Sleep’ from his own album Blunderbuss.

1bSCGVnnijnSf8R9maUeJ9.name: Camille Yarbrough
f: Nina Simone admired her and covered her songs onstage.
Journalist Kevin Powell called Camille Yarbrough's The Iron Pot Cooker a precursor to The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill.
She started dancing late, at about sixteen, and was twenty when she joined Katherine Dunham's company.
In 1971 she was co-starring in To Be Young, Gifted and Black.
Her 1979 children's book Cornrows, illustrated by Carole Byard, won the Coretta Scott King Award.

3lnWfdMG9U0oVMC15SEbB5.name: BODEGA
f: Their album Our Brand Could Be Yr Life reworks Bodega Bay's 33-track 2015 album, for which, Ben Hozie said, every instrument was recorded into a MacBook's internal mic.
They pulled out of the 2024 South by Southwest festival, citing its financial ties with the US Army and RTX Corporation.
They named their album Our Brand Could Be Yr Life after Michael Azerrad's punk history Our Band Could Be Your Life.
Their first album, Endless Scroll (2018), was produced by Parquet Courts member Austin Brown.
Bodega took their name from the term New Yorkers use for small corner shops.

6jQ9UtYXqNfVnPkrH1Xxwi.name: Maxine Nightingale
f: She took up session singing, which she said was easy to do in the evenings while her baby slept; her vocal on Al Matthews' ‘Fool’ caught Pierre Tubbs's attention.
She spent about 18 months in the West End's Hair from 1969, understudying Sheila, then played Sheila in Germany and appeared in Jesus Christ Superstar and Godspell.
At thirteen, she and a friend dropped in on the band Unisound rehearsing; they asked her to sing, and she joined them on the British cabaret circuit.
Overlooked as a UK single, her ‘Lead Me On’ topped Billboard's Easy Listening chart in July 1979 and reached No. 5 on the Hot 100.

3M8NUieZuEOMs0Hf210w4n.name: Van Dyke Parks
f: He suggested the title of the Beach Boys' Smile, and the terms of his collaboration with Brian Wilson included Wilson buying him a $5,000 Volvo.
He played piano at the Troubadour alongside Danny Hutton, and later named Hutton's band Three Dog Night.
In the early 1950s, at the American Boychoir School in Princeton, he sang under conductors Arturo Toscanini, Thomas Beecham and Eugene Ormandy.
As a child actor, he played little Tommy Borden in early ‘lost episodes’ of The Honeymooners and appeared in The Swan (1956), starring Grace Kelly.
His first paid recording work was arranging ‘The Bare Necessities’ for Disney's The Jungle Book (1967), a commission from Terry Gilkyson.

6i6WlGzQtXtz7GcC5H5st5.name: 10cc
f: Before 10cc, Eric Stewart, Kevin Godley and Lol Creme had a two-million-selling hit as Hotlegs with ‘Neanderthal Man’, which began as a test of drum layering.
10cc got their name from Jonathan King, who, Eric Stewart recalled, had had a weird dream the night before.
Eric Stewart offered Apple Records the band's ‘Waterfall’, recorded in early 1972, then waited months for a note saying it wasn't commercial enough to release as a single.
The band's four members agreed to split royalties four ways, Eric Stewart said, no matter who wrote the song.
Kevin Godley and Lol Creme left the band in 1976 to develop an electronic music device called ‘The Gizmo’.

485uL27bPomh29R4JmQehQ.name: Bob Seger
f: He heavily rewrote the lyrics of ‘Old Time Rock and Roll’ but didn't take a one-third writing credit, which he regretted after Risky Business made it famous.
Glenn Frey was meant to sing ‘Shakedown’ but called his old Michigan friend Bob Seger instead, landing him an Oscar nomination and a No. 1 hit.
In 1968 he signed with Capitol Records, turning down Motown, which had offered more money.
His ‘Rosalie’ was about CKLW music director Rosalie Trombley, and Thin Lizzy later recorded it.
His first original song, ‘The Lonely One’, cut with his band the Decibels at Del Shannon's studio in 1961, aired just once on an Ann Arbor station.

0Wkm45quqfx3NepJpXDvwE.name: Superorganism
f: Orono Noguchi recorded her vocals for the band's first song in her school dorm room, straight into her MacBook, while her roommate was in the bathroom.
Early rumours had the band down as the side project of someone like Tame Impala's Kevin Parker or Gorillaz's Damon Albarn.
Their first single, ‘Something for Your M.I.N.D.’, was on the FIFA 18 soundtrack and in the season three premiere of Legion, in which the band played themselves.
On ‘Relax’, cans being cracked open are like a snare drum, band member Harry said.
An enlarged image of member Soul's face (he is Earl Ho) often takes his place in the band's group photographs.

57kIMCLPgkzQlXjblX7XXP.name: Phosphorescent
f: Matthew Houck, who records as Phosphorescent, spent two years building and wiring his studio, Spirit Sounds, himself, starting from a raw garage with echoing rafters.
His ‘Song for Zula’ was used in the films The Spectacular Now and The Amazing Spider-Man 2, and in the series finale of Superstore.
On the title of his album Muchacho, he recalled being alone in Mexico and half-remembering a Pablo Neruda line: something like ‘This is how it is, muchacho.’
In 2009 he made a Willie Nelson tribute, To Willie, inspired by Nelson's Lefty Frizzell tribute To Lefty from Willie.
His 2024 album Revelator was the first to include a song not written by him, by his partner and collaborator Jo Schornikow.

0JqRJZzARcjmH60HwUenow.name: Fox Academy
f: By 2020, Michael Todd Berland and Christian Novelli had been making “drowsy and adventurous indie rock” together as Fox Academy for about a decade.
Stereogum found their bedroom pop “a bit more woodsy on average”, with lots of pop culture references and low-key humour despite the melancholy.
Their releases include albums called Joseph's Deli & Lottery and Angel Hair, and tracks titled ‘Popeyes Bag’, ‘Property Brothers’ and ‘NASCAR’.
Jordana added vocals and violin to their 2019 track ‘Luck’, which Michael Todd Berland and Christian Novelli wrote and recorded themselves.

62pBNClOEZJEyRXrzC2CtI.name: The Apache Relay
f: They took their name from a race-competition scene in the film Heavyweights.
They opened Mumford & Sons tour dates, and their song ‘Power Hungry Animals’ was used in the 2013 comedy film The Way Way Back.
Formed in a dorm at Belmont University, they released the concept album 1988 in 2009 as Michael Ford Jr. & the Apache Relay.
They recorded Bruce Springsteen's ‘Cover Me’ for the tribute album Dead Man's Town: A Tribute to Born in the U.S.A.

19eLuQmk9aCobbVDHc6eek.name: Louis Armstrong
f: He played so loudly on his early recordings with Joe ‘King’ Oliver that he had to stand 15 feet from Oliver, in a far corner of the room.
His recording of ‘Melancholy Blues’ is on the Voyager Golden Record, the sample of Earth's sights and sounds sent into space.
He wore a Star of David to the end of his life, partly in memory of the Karnoffskys, the Lithuanian Jewish family who had helped raise him.
He could blow 200 high Cs in a row, and as his reputation grew other musicians challenged him to cutting contests.
He called his time in Fate Marable's riverboat band, which made its players learn to sight-read, ‘going to the University’.

3uuQLSmKyXSXIStTYGKLrT.name: Freddie Scott
f: In 1962 he cut Gerry Goffin and Carole King's ‘Hey, Girl’ as a demo for Chuck Jackson, then recorded it himself when Jackson missed the session.
His recording of Bert Berns's ‘Are You Lonely for Me’ reputedly took over 100 takes, then spent four weeks at No. 1 on the R&B chart.
He studied medicine at the University of Rhode Island and Paine College, but began singing again with the Swanee Quintet Juniors and gave up his medical career.
As a child he sang in his grandmother's gospel group, Sally Jones & the Gospel Keyes, touring England with them at the age of 12.
Ricky Nelson recorded Freddie Scott's song ‘Baby I'm Sorry’ for his 1957 debut album, Ricky.

3mC1KCuZZSOlN8Z0M56VsV.name: Dobie Gray
f: He persuaded South Africa's apartheid authorities to let him play to integrated audiences, becoming the first artist to do so.
Dobie Gray recorded as Leonard Ainsworth, Larry Curtis and Larry Dennis before Stripe Records suggested a name borrowed from the sitcom The Many Loves of Dobie Gillis.
While in the Los Angeles production of Hair in 1970, he joined the band Pollution, managed by Beverly Hillbillies actor Max Baer Jr.
He left all his musical assets and royalties in trust to St. Jude Children's Research Hospital and the Tennessee School for the Blind.
He said MCA were unsure how to market his albums: ‘They didn't know where to place a black guy in country music.’

3dkbV4qihUeMsqN4vBGg93.name: Al Green
f: As a teenager he was thrown out of the family home after his devoutly religious father caught him listening to Jackie Wilson.
Willie Mitchell hired him in 1969 to sing at a Texas show with his band, signed him to Hi Records, and coached him into finding his own voice.
Born Albert Greene, he dropped the final ‘e’ from his name before releasing his first album on Hi Records.
In 1979 he fell off the stage at a show in Cincinnati, took it as a message from God, and turned to his church and gospel music.
His 2008 album Lay It Down, produced by Ahmir ‘Questlove’ Thompson and James Poyser, was his first top-10 album since the early 1970s.

0SwO7SWeDHJijQ3XNS7xEE.name: MGMT
f: When Columbia Records' A&R department called them to say it was interested, the band thought it was a joke.
They played New Orleans' Voodoo Experience on Halloween 2010 dressed as Scooby-Doo characters, Andrew VanWyngarden as Daphne and Ben Goldwasser as Velma.
They opened for Paul McCartney, an admitted fan, at Fenway Park in Boston on 5 and 6 August 2009.
Before the band played Bonnaroo in 2008 and 2009, Andrew VanWyngarden and Ben Goldwasser had gone to the very first one, in 2002, as fans.
MGMT started out as The Management and shortened the name because another band was already using it.

320TrJub4arztwXRm7kqVO.name: Dr. John
f: Mac Rebennack devised the Dr. John act for his friend Ronnie Barron to front, but Barron dropped out and Rebennack took on the role himself.
His persona was modelled on a real Dr. John, a Senegalese prince and conjure man in New Orleans who claimed to have 15 wives and over 50 children.
Before Dr. John, he had been ‘Professor Bizarre’; he said people also called him ‘Bishop’ or ‘Governor’ before ‘Doctor’ stuck.
Bob Dylan, Bette Midler and Doug Sahm each contributed single lines to the lyrics of Dr. John's 1973 hit ‘Right Place, Wrong Time’.
At 16, then still Mac Rebennack, he was hired as a producer at Ace Records, working with James Booker, Earl King and Jimmy Clanton.

0K1q0nXQ8is36PzOKAMbNe.name: Spoon
f: When their Elektra A&R man Ron Laffitte quit and the label dropped them, the band released a vindictive two-song single titled ‘The Agony of Laffitte’.
When Pete Buttigieg was filmed playing ‘The Way We Get By’ on piano in 2019, they shared it with the comment ‘So this guy can just do anyone's job, huh.’
Their name honours the German krautrock band Can, whose hit ‘Spoon’ was the US theme song for the 1985 film Jagged Edge.
In 2009 the review aggregator Metacritic named them its ‘Top overall artist of the decade’.
Britt Daniel said he wouldn't let the band's music be used to advertise Hummers: ‘I just think they're obnoxious.’

7vpRSadEAzLs0ikY7gAESe.name: Hamilton, Joe Frank & Reynolds
f: WABC DJ Dan Ingram's running joke was to introduce them as ‘Hamilton, Joe, Frank Reynolds and the entire Eyewitness News team’.
A Mystery Science Theater 3000 episode joked that, unseen in print, Hamilton, Joe Frank & Reynolds could be a duo, a trio, a quartet or even a quintet.
Playboy Records made them keep the name though Tommy Reynolds had left; within months they released ‘Fallin' in Love’, a Billboard Hot 100 No. 1.
Dan Hamilton, Joe Frank Carollo and Tommy Reynolds had all played in the T-Bones, whose hit ‘No Matter What Shape (Your Stomach's In)’ was based on an Alka-Seltzer advert.
The back cover of their Fallin' in Love album used the more accurate name Hamilton, Joe Frank & Dennison, which they adopted officially in 1976.

08GQAI4eElDnROBrJRGE0X.name: Fleetwood Mac
f: The Beatles wanted them on Apple Records, but manager Clifford Davis signed them to Warner Bros. instead.
Peter Green and Mick Fleetwood named the band Fleetwood Mac to lure bassist John McVie, who at first chose to keep his steady income with John Mayall.
For the B-side of ‘Man of the World’, Jeremy Spencer fronted the band under the name ‘Earl Vince and the Valiants’.
Peter Green advertised in Melody Maker for a rhythm section to back Danny Kirwan; none of the 300-plus applicants was good enough, so the band took Kirwan instead.
They released ‘Black Magic Woman’ as a single before Santana's cover made it a big hit.

5cMVRrisBpDkXCVG48epED.name: Jenny Lewis
f: Asked by Blake Sennett to sing backing vocals, she refused to join Rilo Kiley unless she could sing lead.
At 11, she was a contestant on the CBS game show Card Sharks, winning $500 but losing her match.
She wanted to call Rilo Kiley Love's Way, after her parents' Las Vegas lounge act, but Blake Sennett ‘didn't go for it’.
She played one of Lucy's grandchildren in Lucille Ball's short-lived 1986 sitcom Life With Lucy.
She voiced the assistant director in Disney's animated film Bolt (2008) and provided its song ‘Barking at the Moon’.

2vQavlZtDA660mnZotYIto.name: Link Wray
f: Pete Townshend of the Who once said he would never have picked up a guitar if it hadn’t been for Link Wray and ‘Rumble’.
His 1958 instrumental ‘Rumble’ was banned in New York and Boston for fear it would incite teenage gang violence.
He is credited with inventing the power chord; AllMusic’s Cub Koda said his early instrumentals laid the blueprints for ‘heavy metal, thrash, you name it’.
Bob Dylan name-checks him in ‘Sign Language’, the song he recorded as a duet with Eric Clapton in 1975.
He and his brothers Ray and Doug drove cabs by day and worked at nightclubs by night in the Portsmouth and Norfolk, Virginia, area.

5g2n2H9ndqvejERtwZ1rHh.name: The Rascals
f: As a stunt, their promoters put ‘The Rascals are coming!’ on the Shea Stadium scoreboard as the Beatles opened their 1965 tour; Brian Epstein had it removed.
Their $15,000 deal made them the first white-only act signed to Atlantic Records, then a label of mainly black artists.
They were known for refusing to tour on segregated bills; their 1968 No. 1 ‘People Got to Be Free’ was a plea for racial tolerance.
Paul McCartney was so excited by their UK debut at London’s Scotch of St James on 1 December 1966 that he also went to their show the next night.
They were renamed the Young Rascals to avoid conflict after Borrah Minnevitch’s and Johnny Puleo’s Harmonica Rascals objected to them recording as the Rascals.

3GHKajYkw1Btlzib5wRpHf.name: Innovations
f: The group’s Javier Guerrero was the son of Manuel A. Guerrero, founder of the Peruvian label Discos MAG.
Ernesto Samamé, who backed Javier Guerrero on the group’s single, was bassist in We All Together, led by Guerrero’s brother Carlos, and a member of Laghonia and Fe 59.
They made only one record, a single so scarce that its first reissue was billed as ‘uber-rare’.

2jgPkn6LuUazBoBk6vvjh5.name: The Zombies
f: In 1969 two fake Zombies line-ups toured at the same time; the Texas one featured Dusty Hill and Frank Beard, soon to be members of ZZ Top.
After the band split, Colin Blunstone worked for a time in the burglary claims section of the Sun Alliance insurance company before going solo.
Paul Arnold came up with the name the Zombies; Colin Blunstone admitted he didn’t really know what a zombie was.
Among their early US gigs were Murray the K’s Christmas shows at the Brooklyn Fox Theatre, where they played seven performances a day.
Their first hit, ‘She’s Not There’, peaked at No. 12 in the UK, their only UK Top 40 hit, but climbed to No. 2 in the US.

5dHfLBNU8zoypgKefzEB1c.name: Pomplamoose
f: The duo's Jack Conte announced the launch of Patreon, co-founded with Samuel Yam, on 7 May 2013.
They sold grapefruit-scented bath soap at their merch table, a nod to their name, a phonetic spelling of the French word for grapefruit.
Their ‘VideoSongs’ follow two rules set by Jack Conte: no lip-syncing to instruments or voice, and no sound you don’t at some point see being made.
Allee Willis offered to write them a song after hearing their cover of Earth, Wind & Fire’s ‘September’; they recorded ‘Jungle Animal’ with her in 2010.
In 2010 they gave a free album download to anyone who bought a book for a Richmond, California charter school; the drive paid for over 11,000 books.

3ir2pF2mkiEWqyPenKTh5e.name: Indigo De Souza
f: On ‘Real Pain’, she put crowdsourced recordings of screams in the chorus, to show how everyone’s experience of pain connects them.
Her mother paints her album covers; the one for Any Shape You Take shows an apocalyptic supermarket overgrown with greenery.
Hurricane Helene mostly destroyed her house while she was on tour in 2024; she has since moved to Los Angeles and says she’s written a more grunge-centred record.
Her lyrics and art often set nature against grocery stores, which she sees as a symbol of feeling out of touch with humanity.
She self-released her first album, I Love My Mom, in 2018; Saddle Creek Records discovered it and gave it a proper release in 2021.

0vIme0FGc4SmFByKiV27tw.name: ARTHUR
f: He hated the mandolin his dad bought him at nine or ten; later he borrowed his brother’s bass for a school concert miming Journey’s ‘Don’t Stop Believin’’.
Also known as Arthur Shea or William Conall Shea, he was a founding member of the Philadelphia indie band Joy Again.
In 2018 he appeared with the producer Vegyn on Frank Ocean’s midterm elections special of blonded RADIO, chatting politics.
He wrote his single ‘AB’ in a warehouse on a day so cold he could see his breath, recording most of it on an iPhone.
He has toured with Alex G and says he would happily do it again.

04PoYcw0Zcevr7MQC0kzUM.name: bby
f: Benjy Gibson found Jessy Jacquet-Cretides on his For You page; the band first met at Pirate Studios in Dalston on 2 January 2023.
Their frontman Benjy Gibson co-wrote and co-produced Fred again.. and Latin Mafia’s mixtape 9 months & 50 hours, and sang on its breakout track ‘Quiereme’.
They host their own gigs for fans at their east London warehouse; Benjy Gibson says it means they don’t have to ‘deal with sound engineers’.
They earned spots on radio playlists including BBC Radio 1’s, and their debut single, ‘Hotline’, became a Top 20 hit on the US alternative charts.

2IU5UBup85LmAXh5U36DeC.name: The Grass Roots
f: The band’s Creed Bratton went on to become a successful actor, best known for his role in The Office.
They reportedly turned down ‘Love Grows (Where My Rosemary Goes)’ because Rob Grill balked at a song that might seem to be about Warren Entner’s wife, Rosemarie Frankland.
The Grass Roots began as a name on a demo, reflecting young people’s growing interest in marijuana; any radio station that wanted the band would find there was no band.
The band’s Warren Entner, a UCLA film student alongside future Doors members Jim Morrison and Ray Manzarek, met fellow busker Creed Bratton in Israel in 1965.
Warren Entner, who left the band by 1974, later became a successful manager of groups such as Rage Against the Machine and Quiet Riot.

2hO4YtXUFJiUYS2uYFvHNK.name: Traveling Wilburys
f: George Harrison, Jeff Lynne and Tom Petty drove to Anaheim to see Roy Orbison play the Celebrity Theatre, and recruited him shortly before he went on stage.
The word Wilbury came from George Harrison's joke about faulty-equipment errors, “We'll bury 'em in the mix”; he first suggested calling the band the Trembling Wilburys.
They posed as half-brothers: Nelson (George Harrison), Otis (Jeff Lynne), Lucky (Bob Dylan), Lefty (Roy Orbison) and Charlie T. Jr. (Tom Petty) Wilbury.
They made Vol. 1 mostly over ten days in May 1988, writing and recording basic tracks in a circle with acoustic guitars in Dave Stewart's kitchen.
Monty Python's Michael Palin wrote the liner notes for the band's debut album under a pseudonym.

0e86yPdC41PGRkLp2Q1Bph.name: Mother Mother
f: In 2020 the lyrics to their ‘Hayloft’ were the most searched-for song lyrics in the US, and the second most in the world.
Ryan Guldemond started the group in January 2005, while at music school, wanting a band built on vocal-driven pop songs, and recruited his sister Molly Guldemond.
Their debut album had a three-headed rooster on its cover; for the 2007 reissue, retitled Touch Up, it grew to five heads.
Last Gang Records signed the band, then called Mother, after a 2006 Pop Montreal set, and urged a name change to avoid legal issues: hence Mother Mother.
A Toronto Star reviewer said their album Eureka sounded “as if Adam Lambert had joined The Dirty Projectors”.

23E65IfLBGQv0FBrMwCcG2.name: Peter McPoland
f: Before making Big Lucky, he cut himself off from social media and streaming, armed with a flip phone and a reel-to-reel machine resurrected from his uncle's basement.
As a boy he planned to be a folk singer and asked for a banjo for Christmas; his parents got him an electric guitar instead.
An acoustic version of ‘Romeo and Juliet’ that he posted on TikTok in March 2021 passed a million views; that May, Columbia Records signed him.
His 2023 debut album, Piggy, takes its title from a main character in the novel Lord of the Flies.
By 16, he had played Vans Warped Tour and New Voices in Rock at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

2kGBy2WHvF0VdZyqiVCkDT.name: Father John Misty
f: Allowed only secular music with a “spiritual theme”, the teenage Josh Tillman bought Slow Train Coming by convincing his parents Bob Dylan was a “Christian artist”.
He moved to Seattle at 21 and worked at a bakery, recording music at night before his 4:30 am shift.
In 2018 he turned down a Rolling Stone cover, and the magazine told him he was the least famous person to reject the offer.
He joined Fleet Foxes as drummer in 2008, played on Helplessness Blues (2011), and played his last show with them in Tokyo on 20 January 2012.
In 2015 he covered Taylor Swift's ‘Blank Space’ and ‘Welcome to New York’ as a parody of Ryan Adams's covers of her album 1989.

6eJa3zG1QZLRB3xgRuyxbm.name: Dayglow
f: Although Sloan Struble is Dayglow's only member, he calls it a band rather than a solo act, likening it to Tame Impala or Mutemath.
He named Dayglow after the song ‘Day Glo’ by Brazos.
At 11, he began teaching himself guitar, bass, keyboard, synthesiser and drums, and how to produce and mix, using GarageBand.
In 2024 he performed ‘We Are What We Think We Are’ on the children's TV show Yo Gabba Gabbaland.
Before Dayglow, he recorded as Kindred; only one Kindred song, ‘Spent my Life’, reached streaming services, the rest staying on SoundCloud.

7xxsnuyDlv8QUCHLZd2Qlz.name: Outer Limits Recordings
f: Outer Limits Recordings began as Sam Mehran's own fake record company, the original home of his music.
He named his main influences as Ariel Pink, R. Stevie Moore and “basically most music that was recorded before 1990”.
Sam Mehran's alias from 2010 was immediately associated with the early hypnagogic pop and chillwave scene.
The project issued numerous cassettes and limited-edition vinyl discs and, by Sam Mehran's account, lasted until “somewhere in the spring of 2011”.
Music journalist Paul Lester summed up the project as “heavenly hooks and catchy choruses”.

147s6QtLc4KPRmh5YxfpMO.name: Sam Mehran
f: He was rumoured to be working in a New York coffee shop, content with a quiet life; in fact, it was his most prolific period.
He started Test Icicles with Rory Attwell and Devonté Hynes, and later said they hadn't expected the band to last more than two weeks.
His first album as Matrix Metals, Flamingo Breeze, has been described as a pioneering work of vaporwave.
His last work released in his lifetime was co-writing and co-producing Ssion's 2018 album O.
His final album, Cold Brew, was released on 28 July 2021, the third anniversary of his death.

3WKTiixhkaWRexRUs3GKBw.name: Alan Price
f: He was a founding member of the Alan Price Combo, later renamed the Animals, and played organ on ‘The House of the Rising Sun’.
He left the Animals in 1965 over personal and musical differences, and his fear of flying on tour.
His score for Lindsay Anderson's O Lucky Man! (1973), which he also performs on screen, won the 1974 BAFTA for Best Film Music.
Although he supports Sunderland, their rivals Newcastle United often played his version of ‘Blaydon Races’ at matches.
His minor hits ‘Just For You’ (1978) and ‘Baby of Mine’ (1979) were also pressed as red, heart-shaped vinyl discs.

7d7q5Y1p2QWS4QRAhTQR5E.name: Anne Murray
f: She was the first Canadian female solo singer to reach No. 1 in the US, and the first to earn a gold record, with ‘Snowbird’ (1970).
She wasn't offended at being named in South Park's Oscar-nominated ‘Blame Canada’, but turned down singing it at the Oscars, pleading a prior commitment.
On a 1965 University of New Brunswick student record, The Groove, of which 500 were pressed, her name was misspelled “Anne Murry”.
She taught physical education for a year at a high school in Summerside, Prince Edward Island, before joining TV's Singalong Jubilee.
She has won a record 25 Juno Awards, as well as four Grammys.

4chuPfKtATDZvbRLExsTp2.name: Vashti Bunyan
f: She and Robert Lewis bought an old wagon and a horse from a Romany traveller and set off on a 650-mile trek from South London to Skye.
She said seeing Joni Mitchell sing on television made her lose all confidence, and she gave up music for about 30 years.
She was expelled from Oxford's Ruskin School of Drawing and Fine Art in 1964 for learning guitar and writing songs instead of art.
Her first single, Mick Jagger and Keith Richards' ‘Some Things Just Stick in Your Mind’, came out in June 1965 with Jimmy Page on guitar.
Devendra Banhart, a longtime fan, reportedly writes her name on his arm before some concerts.

3HC7NcxQx2Yk0fWoRKJ0xF.name: Jefferson Starship
f: The name Jefferson Starship first appeared on Paul Kantner's 1970 album Blows Against the Empire, which was nominated for science fiction's Hugo Award in 1971.
In 1978 they recorded ‘Light the Sky on Fire’ for television's Star Wars Holiday Special.
Their lead guitarist Craig Chaquico was a teenager when his high-school English teacher, Jack Traylor, introduced him to Paul Kantner.
When Paul Kantner quit the band in 1984 and took legal action over the name, the remaining members carried on as Starship.
RCA reportedly spent $500,000 on the band's Earth (1978), and about 400 AM and FM stations aired it in full in RCA's most extensive radio promotion.

3Q6OOkfssqoMSTtl11J5Uk.name: Love
f: They lived communally in ‘the Castle’, a dilapidated mansion the band could stay in as long as they did the maintenance and paid the taxes.
Led by songwriter Arthur Lee, they were one of the first racially diverse American rock bands.
Their Forever Changes (1967) reached No. 24 in the UK but only No. 154 in the US; in 2011 it joined the Library of Congress's National Recording Registry.
They were Elektra Records' first rock act, and had a minor hit in 1966 with Burt Bacharach and Hal David's ‘My Little Red Book’.
Love were first called the Grass Roots, until Arthur Lee renamed the band when another group of that name appeared.

76o4kCpWMmBGl8jIYfRHTk.name: Ken Dodd
f: He made his professional debut in September 1954 at the Nottingham Empire as Professor Yaffle Chucklebutty, Operatic Tenor and Sausage Knotter.
In the 1960s he set a Guinness record by telling 1,500 jokes in three and a half hours at Liverpool's Royal Court Theatre, where audiences came in shifts.
His ‘Tears’ topped the UK chart for five weeks in 1965, the year's biggest hit in Britain, and sold over a million copies in the UK alone.
He caught the show-business bug from a comic advert inviting readers to ‘send 6d in stamps and become a ventriloquist!’; he sent off for the book.
He played Yorick, seen in silent flashback, in Kenneth Branagh's 1996 film of Hamlet.

6PAt558ZEZl0DmdXlnjMgD.name: Eric Clapton
f: His nickname ‘Slowhand’ came from Giorgio Gomelsky, a pun on the slow handclapping audiences gave while he replaced broken strings on stage.
In 1967 an unknown admirer spray-painted ‘Clapton is God’ on a wall in Islington; he was reportedly embarrassed by it.
He left the Yardbirds on the day ‘For Your Love’ came out; Jimmy Page declined to replace him out of loyalty and suggested Jeff Beck.
Fans call Blues Breakers – John Mayall – With Eric Clapton ‘The Beano Album’, because its cover shows Clapton reading the children's comic The Beano.
He first played the Royal Albert Hall with the Yardbirds in December 1964 and has played there over 200 times, likening it to ‘playing in my front room’.

2G8UkPZnQ8i78L8TfqP1X6.name: Christian Leave
f: His parents are pastors, and until he got an iPod he wasn't really allowed secular music; he couldn't even listen to the Beatles.
Born Christian Akridge, he named his act after his social media username; he joined Vine in 2014, aged 14, and gained over 800,000 followers.
He wrote, recorded and produced his EP Trilogy entirely in his bedroom.
He first played music as a helping bassist in church; his grandparents sang in the group the Singing Gadberrys.
His debut EP, Hope, released in 2016, attracted over 50 million streams.

3eskO5m0H4yiF64vRySBjr.name: Buffalo Springfield
f: Stephen Stills and Richie Furay spotted Neil Young and Bruce Palmer stuck in traffic on Sunset Boulevard; five days later, the band played their first gig.
Future Buffalo Springfield members Neil Young and Bruce Palmer pawned their band the Mynah Birds' equipment, bought a 1953 Pontiac hearse and drove it to Los Angeles.
Buffalo Springfield took its name from a steamroller parked outside the band's house, made by the Buffalo-Springfield Roller Company.
Before forming the band, Stephen Stills worked as a session musician on the West Coast and auditioned unsuccessfully for the Monkees.
In October 1967 they appeared on the detective series Mannix; Stephen Stills later called it ‘the best sound we ever got’.

4vpDg7Y7fU982Ds30zawDA.name: The Band
f: Garth Hudson agreed to join the Hawks, later the Band, only if each member paid him $10 a week as their instructor and they bought a new Lowrey organ.
At Manchester's Free Trade Hall on 17 May 1966, an audience member shouted ‘Judas!’ at Bob Dylan, who told his backing band, the future Band, to play loud.
Hurt by the hostile reception to Bob Dylan's electric tour, the Band's Levon Helm quit it and spent much of the time on a Gulf of Mexico oil rig.
Ronnie Hawkins fined the Hawks, later the Band, for bringing girlfriends to the clubs, fearing it would cut the number of ‘available’ girls at his shows.
Levon Helm said the name ‘The Band’ suited them because, to various frontmen and to the locals in Woodstock, they had always simply been ‘the band’.

0oSGxfWSnnOXhD2fKuz2Gy.name: David Bowie
f: David Jones became David Bowie to avoid confusion with the Monkees' Davy Jones, naming himself after pioneer James Bowie and the knife he popularised.
He said that on hearing Little Richard's ‘Tutti Frutti’, from a pile of American 45s his father brought home, he had ‘heard God’.
He created the first modern celebrity bond, ‘Bowie Bonds’, and through his website BowieNet was one of the first artists to deal with fans directly online.
His mother gave him a Grafton saxophone in 1961, and he was soon taking lessons from baritone saxophonist Ronnie Ross.
At Bromley Technical High School, he spent lunch breaks playing Buddy Holly songs with schoolmate Peter Frampton.

48c9PKsgH8QMkAN6pg6Xz8.name: Chaparelle
f: The band began with a tip from an ex: Zella Day's former boyfriend suggested she check out singer-songwriter Jesse Woods's music.
The band's Zella Day became a fan of Jesse Woods's 2021 album Wimberley, messaged him, and first met him when she came to Austin for ACL.
They took George Jones and Tammy Wynette as their ‘North Star’, Jesse Woods says.
Beau Bedford, the band's third member, produced their debut record and plays guitar; Zella Day says he ‘really kind of acts as the tiebreaker’.

100sLnojEpcadRx4edEBA6.name: Zella Day
f: Her cover of the White Stripes' ‘Seven Nation Army’ reached No. 1 on Hype Machine's charts and passed 50 million Spotify plays.
She released her debut album, Powered by Love, independently in 2009 at the age of 14; a family friend funded and recorded it.
She sang ‘For Free’ with Weyes Blood and Lana Del Rey at the Hollywood Bowl in 2019; the trio's studio version is on Chemtrails over the Country Club.
She named her 2015 album Kicker after the old Arizona mining town where her parents married.
She was immersed in the café and art space her parents helped create in Pinetop-Lakeside, Arizona, and wrote her first songs soon after taking up guitar at nine.

5I6MzhNEMk27cZsCqGAIYo.name: The Youngbloods
f: Their ‘Get Together’ stalled at No. 62 in 1967; two years later, after use in brotherhood campaigns on radio and TV, it was re-released and reached the Top 5.
Johnny Carson reportedly barred them from The Tonight Show; Jesse Colin Young said they refused to play when told to do only ‘Get Together’.
They answered Merle Haggard's ‘Okie from Muskogee’ with ‘Hippie from Olema’, on their 1971 album Good & Dusty.
Their frontman Jesse Colin Young built his stage name from the outlaws Jesse James and Cole Younger and Formula One engineer Colin Chapman.
The Youngbloods took their name from Youngblood (1965), the second solo album by Jesse Colin Young.

4qmHkMxr6pTWh5Zo74odpH.name: Elvis Costello & The Attractions
f: The Attractions’ keyboardist Steve Nieve, born Stephen Nason, got his stage name from tourmate Ian Dury, who was astonished when Nason innocently asked, ‘What’s a groupie?’
Asked why Bruce Thomas didn’t play with the Attractions at their 2003 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction, Elvis Costello replied, ‘I only work with professional musicians.’
Elvis Costello cut his debut with the American band Clover; This Year’s Model (1978) was his first with the Attractions, whose Bruce Thomas and Pete Thomas are unrelated.
In 1980 the Attractions recorded an album of their own, Mad About the Wrong Boy, with songs by all three members and Roger Bechirian producing.

3d2pb1dHTm8b61zAGVUVvO.name: Mick Jagger
f: He met Keith Richards again at Dartford station on 17 October 1961; the Chuck Berry and Muddy Waters records Jagger carried revealed a shared interest in rhythm and blues.
He studied finance and accounting at the London School of Economics on a government grant, and seriously considered becoming a journalist or a politician.
His father, Basil ‘Joe’ Jagger, was a gymnast and PE teacher who helped popularise basketball in Britain.
He opened one Rolling Stones concert by reading from Percy Bysshe Shelley’s ‘Adonaïs’, after which thousands of butterflies were released in Brian Jones’s memory.
His band first played as the Rollin’ Stones, named after a Muddy Waters song, at London’s Marquee Club on 12 July 1962.

1QyjHJQb3WeWFxXaNLpLOw.name: Anna Ash
f: Her homespun four-song demo CD came wrapped in brown paper sewn with green thread, crediting her with ‘banjo, vocals, mouth trumpet, and bird thoughts’.
She wrote her song ‘Popularity’ in summer 2020, after fleeing California, while living in a trailer in her mother’s backyard.
Her music has featured in the TV series Masters of Sex and Billions, and in the docuseries Helter Skelter: An American Myth.
She launched a Kickstarter in December 2010 to fund These Holy Days, planning an EP; it became her first full-length album.
She does a lot of her own engineering on her records, including the editing and recording of overdubs.

1gR0gsQYfi6joyO1dlp76N.name: Justice
f: They first came to prominence with a 2003 remix of Simian’s ‘Never Be Alone’, made for a Paris college radio station’s remix contest; it got them signed to Ed Banger.
They made a mix for the Fabriclive series in 2008, but Fabric rejected it; Xavier de Rosnay said, ‘They weren’t ready for something like this.’
They described their second album, Audio, Video, Disco, as ‘a progressive rock record, played by guys that don’t know how to play’.
Their first tracks were for Musclorvision’s ‘Hits Up to You’, a concept compilation of songs designed to sound like Eurovision entries.
Their remix of MGMT’s ‘Electric Feel’ won the 2009 Grammy Award for Best Remixed Recording, Non-Classical.

5INjqkS1o8h1imAzPqGZBb.name: Tame Impala
f: Tame Impala began in 2007 as Kevin Parker’s home-recording project; the tracks he posted on Myspace won him a worldwide deal with Modular Recordings in July 2008.
His Lonerism became the first Australian album to win NME’s album of the year.
The cover of Lonerism is Kevin Parker’s own photograph of the Jardin du Luxembourg in Paris.
iTunes accidentally put his debut album, Innerspeaker, on sale in the UK on 12 May, weeks before its official 28 June release.
His first top-ten hit on the US Billboard Hot 100 was a remix of ‘Dracula’ with Jennie of Blackpink.

1GiGmnJBIwKiXV8AbjuJ9P.name: Life in Film
f: Burberry’s Christopher Bailey sought them out after they sent a video of their song ‘Carla’ to a YouTube channel; their ‘Alleyway’ later fronted the Burberry Acoustic initiative.
They played ‘The Idiot’ to open Vogue’s Fashion Night Out on 9 September 2010.
Their single ‘The Idiot’ was produced by Mike Crossey at Liverpool’s Motor Museum studio, and its video was made with the designer Kate Moross.

0h1gX589xBKUCijeC8Bewy.name: Charlotte Adigéry
f: Her Creole-language song ‘Paténipat’ was used in the trailer for The New Pope, HBO's 2020 series with John Malkovich.
In 2019 she released Yin Yang Self-Meditation, a cassette single limited to 300 copies, using stream of consciousness to explore racism and being an artist.
In 2016 she sang on ‘The Best Thing’, from the soundtrack to the film Belgica, scored by Soulwax's David and Stephen Dewaele.
She also records as WWWater, a rawer, more punk project.

0dSnTqwXok006MwsjjlzUl.name: Bolis Pupul
f: Bolis Pupul's name comes from how his grandmother pronounced his first name, Boris, and from ‘pupul’, a sound his father repeated to help him fall asleep.
He and his sister Sarah played in the Shitz, a fictional band in the 2016 film Belgica, recording two Soulwax-written songs for its soundtrack.
He is the son of Belgian cartoonist Luc ‘Kamagurka’ Zeebroek, and has said he would take up drawing if his music career ever ended.
He played in synthpop band Hong Kong Dong with his sister and her husband; they reached the finals of Humo's Rock Rally in 2008.
His solo debut, Letter to Yu (2024), was inspired by his mother and his Chinese heritage; the video for lead single ‘Completely Half’ was shot in Hong Kong.

5hE6NCoobhyEu6TRSbjOJY.name: Fever Ray
f: Their ‘If I Had a Heart’ became the opening theme of the TV series Vikings, and was also used in Breaking Bad and Person of Interest.
They often perform behind a gauze screen that partly hides them from the audience, using masks, face and body paint and intricate costumes.
Their second album, Plunge, came out without prior announcement, and won Karin Dreijer and its producers the 2018 Swedish Grammis for Producer of the Year.
They made their film debut in Maggie Gyllenhaal's The Bride!, performing in a scene set in an underground nightclub.

13peDbMKVZpn5nanRC96WJ.name: Thumpasaurus
f: Their line-up lists Ben Benjamin on ‘visuals/pancakes’, alongside Lucas Tamaren, Henry Was, Logan Kane, Henry Solomon and Paul Cornish.
Their John Travolta imagery began when Ben Benjamin, who creates their live visuals, threw Travolta images and clips behind the band at a show.
