They started as a folk band playing house parties; Henry Was called their style part of a reaction to music school, where there's always a right and wrong answer.
They made their international late-night TV debut in France, on Alain Chabat's Le Late, right after the 2022 World Cup.

2dBj3prW7gP9bCCOIQeDUf.name: Danger Mouse
f: Brian Burton took the name Danger Mouse from the English cartoon series and performed in a mouse outfit because he was too shy to show his face.
In 2006 he and Banksy replaced 500 copies of Paris Hilton's album in British shops with altered artwork and a 40-minute instrumental.
Blocked by a dispute with EMI, he planned to issue Dark Night of the Soul as a blank CD-R labelled as containing no music ‘for legal reasons’.
He made The Grey Album, setting Jay-Z's The Black Album over samples of the Beatles' White Album, just for friends; it spread online and made his name.
While living in New Cross and working at the Rose pub near London Bridge, he sent a demo to Lex Records, which signed him.

4fUoc6Qd6emrChaXSkS91n.name: Jemini
f: The Guardian put him and Danger Mouse on its list of the Forty Best Bands in the US, saying Ghetto Pop Life's lyrical intelligence bore comparison to prime-time Public Enemy.
A remix of a Danger Mouse and Jemini record featured CeeLo Green; beats Danger Mouse shared when they met for it led to Gnarls Barkley.
Jemini the Gifted One, the Brooklyn rapper Thomas Smith, had his debut single, ‘Funk Soul Sensation’, produced by Organized Konfusion.
He released ‘Brooklyn Basquiat’ with Danger Mouse in 2023, and died on 27 March 2025.

320EPCSEezHt1rtbfwH6Ck.name: The Monkees
f: Stephen Stills recommended Peter Tork to the band's producers at Stills's own audition; Tork had been working as a busboy.
Michael Nesmith turned up to his audition with his laundry; the woollen hat he wore on his motorcycle earned him the early nickname ‘Wool Hat’.
They weren't even given a copy of their second album, More of the Monkees, released without their knowledge; they had to buy it from a record shop.
Bob Rafelson and Bert Schneider conceived the band for an NBC sitcom, and first planned to cast an existing folk rock group, the Lovin' Spoonful.
Michael Nesmith, Peter Tork and Micky Dolenz were chosen from 437 applicants to join Davy Jones in the band's television cast.

2kRFetyCeU3r24DVyTZVFx.name: Surfbort
f: Dani Miller started the group by lying that she was in a band when someone at a Together Pangea gig mentioned booking a show.
Surfbort took its name from the Beyoncé song ‘Drunk in Love’.
In 2019, Dani Miller's three bandmates were 50-something veterans of the 1980s West Texas punk scene.
They starred in Gucci's Pre-Fall 2019 campaign, photographed in Sicily, after playing the opening of Gucci's Wooster Street store in New York.
Members of Blondie have named them as one of their favourite bands.

1jFVu6Z7wmwywivOeBTSIV.name: Miya Folick
f: She was raised a Jōdo Shinshū Buddhist and learned to play taiko drums in a church group.
At her 2019 Tiny Desk Concert, she said she had been watching Tiny Desk Concerts since before she even played music.
She studied acting at New York University, graduated from the University of Southern California's School of Theatre, and learned guitar from a high-school friend during a gap semester.
In 2022 she sang on American Football's cover of ‘Fade Into You’.

2VPvWVAiP9GICmwh4bLUuE.name: Sahara Hotnights
f: Drummer Josephine Forsman named Sahara Hotnights after a horse of that name she bet on while in Australia.
They formed around 1992 ‘due to boredom’, and around 1995 won a battle of the bands whose prize was a chance to record in a studio.
Their line-up has never changed: singer Maria Andersson, drummer Josephine Forsman and the sisters Jennie and Johanna Asplund on guitar and bass.
They named their second album, Jennie Bomb (2001), after their guitarist Jennie Asplund.
Their ‘Alright Alright (Here's My Fist Where's the Fight?)’ is used in Cheaper by the Dozen, Stormbreaker and New York Minute, and on the Jackass: The Movie soundtrack.

5mZC7ndY6oGMxJentRwsuV.name: Young Fathers
f: Six tracks on the T2 Trainspotting soundtrack feature the band; Danny Boyle called ‘Only God Knows’, written for the film, ‘the heartbeat for the film’.
They won the 2014 Mercury Prize with their debut album, Dead.
Alloysious Massaquoi, Kayus Bankole and Graham ‘G’ Hastings played nightclubs as teenagers and released a single as 3Style in 2005, before becoming Young Fathers in 2008.
They composed the score for Danny Boyle's horror sequel 28 Years Later, announcing it in May 2025.
They have featured on two FIFA soundtracks: ‘Border Girl’ on FIFA 19 and ‘Rice’ on FIFA 23.

7kAZYW5e5hQHYGQ0XHYhns.name: Mustard Service
f: They took their name from a band name generator; Marco Rivero said the other contenders were Milk Inequality and Johnny's Trashcan.
They cite the Beach Boys as their main influence, and reviewers often call their music ‘beachy’.
All of their members have Latin heritage and speak some Spanish, and the band often borrows from Latin music, especially bossa nova.
In autumn 2018 they joined the Madrid band Hinds on a sixteen-date US tour, and were praised for their energetic shows.

12fRkVfO2fUsz1QHgDAG3g.name: Julia Jacklin
f: Inspired by Britney Spears, she took classical singing lessons at 10, then joined a high-school band covering Avril Lavigne and Evanescence.
She worked in an essential oils factory to save up to record with producer Ben Edwards, having been inspired by Aldous Harding's debut album.
In 2025 she became lead vocalist of Binspoon, a Grinspoon tribute act.
She has co-directed all her music videos, in a style she says is inspired by Swedish photographer Lars Tunbjörk's pictures of the mundane and absurd in modern life.
In 2014 she formed the garage band Phantastic Ferniture with Elizabeth Hughes on guitar and Ryan K Brennan on drums.

0Lpr5wXzWLtDWm1SjNbpPb.name: Todd Rundgren
f: He organised the first interactive television concert in 1978, designed the first colour graphics tablet in 1980 and made the first interactive album, No World Order, in 1993.
After their first meeting, Laura Nyro asked him to be her band leader, but Nazz had just signed a record contract and he couldn't leave the band.
Albert Grossman promised him he would become the ‘highest-paid producer in the world’, which later came true.
He was due to produce Janis Joplin's album Pearl, but the plan fell through because the two could not get along.
He wrote both sides of Nazz's debut single, July 1968's ‘Open My Eyes’ backed with ‘Hello It's Me’.

5O35zGUolf87RATk2NgSD3.name: Hether
f: He made ends meet driving for Lyft and serving as music director for a Russian Pentecostal church.
He was playing San Diego bars with jazz greats until Rodney Jerkins brought him to Los Angeles to play on tracks for Britney Spears and Justin Bieber.
Paul Castelluzzo had never sung before the night he wrote his first song as Hether, after a world tour in Romeo Santos's live band ended.
He has writing credits and plays guitar on ‘Time’ by the Free Nationals, Mac Miller and Kali Uchis.

2u7xZP39dtED9EuRX9MUwu.name: Orange Juice
f: They recorded their debut single, ‘Falling and Laughing’, in eight hours; Edwyn Collins blamed its slightly out-of-tune sound on the band being unable to afford a guitar tuner.
Alan Horne and Edwyn Collins accosted John Peel outside the BBC with a copy of the band's first single; Peel at first called their music ‘curious’.
The B-side of their debut single, the instrumental ‘Moscow’, was recorded as a tentative theme tune for the 1980 Moscow Olympics.
Coming on as support act on 11 December 1980, they became the first band ever to play Rock City in Nottingham.
The band began in 1976 as the Nu Sonics, named after the Burns Nu-Sonic guitar Edwyn Collins bought for £20 at 16.

4Q82S0VzF8qlCb4PnSDurj.name: Brian Wilson
f: At 15, he worked part-time sweeping at a jewellery store, his only paid job before his success in music.
He named an early group with his cousin Mike Love ‘Carl and the Passions’ to entice his brother Carl Wilson into joining.
He was given an electric bass days before the Beach Boys' major live debut on New Year's Eve 1961, prompting Al Jardine to switch to rhythm guitar.
He co-wrote ‘Surf City’ with Jan Berry; in July 1963 it became his first composition to top the US charts.
After signing with Capitol Records in 1962, he became the first pop musician credited for writing, arranging, producing and performing his own material.

4gHcu2JoaXJ0mV4aNPCd7N.name: Benny Sings
f: Tim van Berkestijn made beats as Benny V Kreamtits, then became Benny Sings in 1999 on joining the Dutch hip hop group Abstract Dialect as bassist.
He has said he writes 200 songs a year to find the gold, and that his goal was always to be an unsuccessful songwriter.
He wanted to play saxophone, but the saxophone shop said his hands were too small, so he had to start on clarinet.
He helped write Rex Orange County’s 2017 single ‘Loving Is Easy’ and composed songs for the anime Carole & Tuesday.
His Amsterdam studio, tucked under a medieval bridge on a canal, was once used for storing boats.

3UNrI3SG1l2ezKikxQ2zuk.name: Edgar Winter
f: He was the first person to strap a keyboard around his neck, doing so in live performances of his instrumental ‘Frankenstein’.
Edgar Winter Group drummer Chuck Ruff named ‘Frankenstein’ after the massive editing of its studio recording; its working title was ‘The Double Drum Song’.
Ukulele was his first instrument; he later became adept on bass, guitar, keyboards, drums and saxophone.
As a session musician he played saxophone on Meat Loaf’s ‘All Revved Up with No Place to Go’ and Tina Turner’s ‘Simply the Best’.
He produced, arranged and performed on Mission Earth (1986), an album whose lyrics and music were written by Scientology founder L. Ron Hubbard.

2Tglaf8nvDzwSQnpSrjLHP.name: Cuco
f: He first released music as Heavy Trip, then switched to Cuco, a nickname his mother gave him as a child.
He played alongside saxophonist Kenny G at Coachella in April 2018.
He signed with Interscope Records in March 2019, after a bidding war that lasted two years.
After his first single, ‘Lo Que Siento’, took off (it has passed 400 million Spotify streams), he dropped out of Santa Monica City College after a year.
Before he was 15, he had tried trumpet, guitar, keyboard, drums, bass guitar, mellophone and French horn.

56UIK6wmbbxuQ6VA20vrWD.name: Lola Marsh
f: The duo was conceived at Gil Landau’s birthday party in February 2011, when the members began playing songs on his father’s old guitar.
Their cover of ‘Somethin’ Stupid’ featured in the 2018 Better Call Saul episode of the same name.
Their singer Yael Shoshana Cohen was a waitress for ten years, writing on napkins when the place was empty.
Nylon said their first single, ‘Sirens’ (2015), seemed ready-made for Quentin Tarantino’s next film score.
Lola Marsh got its name when someone suggested ‘Lola’ and ‘Marsh’ and the duo combined them.

6CWTBjOJK75cTE8Xv8u1kj.name: Feist
f: She worked the back of the stage at shows by her flatmate Merrill Nisker, alias Peaches, using a sock puppet and calling herself ‘Bitch Lap Lap’.
At 15 she founded the Calgary punk band Placebo, which won a battle of the bands and opened the 1993 festival Infest, featuring the Ramones.
At 12 she was one of 1,000 dancers in the Calgary Winter Olympics opening ceremony, which she cites as inspiration for the ‘1234’ video.
In Broken Social Scene she sang on many tracks after de facto bandleader Kevin Drew forbade her to play guitar.
She sang a counting version of ‘1234’ on Sesame Street in 2008 and called working with the Muppets a career highlight.

4GO3ufZJ7YsEnQ3PiML2Dg.name: Shirley Ellis
f: Her novelty hit ‘The Name Game’ reached US number 3 in 1964 and was later covered by Jessica Lange and the cast of American Horror Story: Asylum.
By 1954 she had written two songs recorded by the Chords.
The Go! Team sampled her ‘Soul Time’ for their single ‘Bottle Rocket’.
She started out in the group the Metronomes and married its lead singer, Alphonso Elliston.
Her ‘I See It, I Like It, I Want It’ featured in a 2023 Walmart commercial, and her ‘The Puzzle Song’ in a 2024 Amazon Prime one.

2M3vnW1p5w4uPRkLYTbvdB.name: Rusted Root
f: The band's singer Michael Glabicki has cited the success of Peter Gabriel’s 1986 album So as an influence on his decision to bring worldbeat into his music.
Their percussion section draws on African, Latin American, Indian and Native American influences.
Their 2012 album, The Movement, was funded by their fans.
They have sold more than three million albums; their 1994 album When I Woke went platinum.
When the band went on indefinite hiatus after touring through 2015, Michael Glabicki formed Uprooted with former members and toured with it into the early 2020s.

0UF7XLthtbSF2Eur7559oV.name: Kavinsky
f: In his fictional backstory, the red-eyed, blue-skinned character crashed his Testarossa in 1986 and returned in 2006 as a zombie making electronic music.
His first single, ‘Testarossa Autodrive’, was inspired by the Ferrari Testarossa; Vincent Belorgey, the man behind the persona, drove one in real life.
He started making music on an old Apple computer from his friend Quentin Dupieux, and said he wrote and recorded all of his EP Teddy Boy on a Yamaha DX7.
Before his music career, he spent years as an actor; he appeared in Quentin Dupieux’s 2007 film Steak, which also used his music.
When he died on 28 July 2026, French president Emmanuel Macron called him ‘a source of French pride forever’.

5GA6j57yIPCBrWk1lTvF9o.name: Lime Garden
f: They describe their sound as ‘wonk pop’, blending disco, pop and surf.
They have said ‘23’, the second single from their 2026 album Maybe Not Tonight, is their favourite of the singles they have recorded.
NME named them one of its top 100 artists for 2022.
They have toured with IDLES, Sunflower Bean and Yard Act, and played Latitude, Reading and Leeds, and Green Man.
The band’s members met at a college in Guildford, studied further at BIMM Brighton, and dropped their earlier name, LIME.

2K13AVg3bFpHSxDM1vJ0qA.name: CSS
f: CSS, short for Cansei de Ser Sexy, took their name from a reported quote in which Beyoncé declared she was ‘tired of being sexy’.
A limited edition of their Brazilian debut album came with a blank CD-R, so buyers could burn a copy to give away as a gift.
Apple used their ‘Music Is My Hot Hot Sex’ in a worldwide iPod advert, a year after the same song promoted the rival Zune player.
They were due to play Lollapalooza on 4 August 2007 but were left stranded at LaGuardia Airport by an overbooking error.
They reformed in 2019 after what was planned as a one-off gig in their hometown, São Paulo.

1PXStuNqw9YDsim4EhMSq7.name: Dan Carey
f: His production for bands on his label Speedy Wunderground, such as Black Country, New Road, Black Midi and Squid, helped create the Windmill scene.
He has five Mercury Prize nominations as a producer, including Black Midi’s Schlagenheim and Fontaines D.C.’s Dogrel in 2019.
He produced and played synthesiser on Wet Leg’s self-titled debut album.
He was one half of Danmass, whose only album, Formfreaks, came out on Dust2Dust in 1999.

77mJc3M7ZT5oOVM7gNdXim.name: Her's
f: They toured with a cardboard cut-out of Pierce Brosnan, whom Stephen Fitzpatrick called the band's ‘spirit animal’ and ‘third member’; Brosnan later paid tribute on Instagram.
Stephen Fitzpatrick and Audun Laading first formed the band as a joke, filming comedic music videos around Liverpool and posting them on YouTube.
The band's Stephen Fitzpatrick and Audun Laading met at the Liverpool Institute for Performing Arts, and Paul McCartney handed them their certificates when they graduated in 2016.
The musician Strawberry Guy, a friend of the band, says he got his stage name from a drunken question asked by Audun Laading.
Five years after Stephen Fitzpatrick and Audun Laading died, their families and friends opened the Friends of Her's fund to fight homelessness in Liverpool.

3WrFJ7ztbogyGnTHbHJFl2.name: The Beatles
f: After a New Year's Day audition, Decca Records rejected them, telling their manager Brian Epstein that ‘guitar groups are on the way out’.
George Harrison won his place as lead guitarist in the band that became the Beatles by playing ‘Raunchy’ on the upper deck of a Liverpool bus.
Stuart Sutcliffe, who bought a bass with money from selling a painting, suggested renaming the future Beatles the Beatals, a tribute to Buddy Holly and the Crickets.
Before settling on their name, they also played as the Rainbows, which Paul McCartney said was because they all had different-coloured shirts and couldn't afford others.
They hold the records for most Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles (20) and most Billboard 200 number-one albums (19).

5fmvGUlMVgmnCn45f1he7d.name: Andrew Gold
f: His recording of ‘Final Frontier’, the Mad About You theme, was used as the wake-up call for the Mars Pathfinder space probe in 1996.
His mother, Marni Nixon, sang for Natalie Wood in West Side Story and Audrey Hepburn in My Fair Lady; his father Ernest Gold won an Oscar for Exodus.
He played most of the instruments on ‘You're No Good’, Linda Ronstadt's only number one on the Billboard Hot 100.
His children's song ‘Spooky, Scary Skeletons’ became a viral hit on YouTube, and New York magazine called it the ‘Internet's Halloween anthem’ in 2019.
His ‘Thank You for Being a Friend’, sung by Cindy Fee, became the opening theme of The Golden Girls in 1985.

5fbhwqYYh4YwUoEs582mq5.name: The Spinners
f: Their bass singer Pervis Jackson was nicknamed ‘Mister 12:45’ after his signature line on ‘They Just Can't Stop It (The Games People Play)’.
During lean years at Motown, they were put to work as road managers, chaperones and chauffeurs for other acts, and even as shipping clerks.
It was Aretha Franklin who suggested they finish their Motown contract and sign with her label, Atlantic Records.
Their first top ten hit, ‘I'll Be Around’, started out as a B-side; radio airplay led Atlantic to flip the single over.
In the UK the Spinners were billed as the Motown Spinners and later the Detroit Spinners, to avoid confusion with a British folk group of the same name.

4Xn6fPXDrarY8LxXWqlE2M.name: Elkie Brooks
f: She formed Vinegar Joe with Pete Gage and Robert Palmer, and her stage shows earned her a reputation as the wild woman of rock 'n' roll.
In the mid-1960s she supported the Beatles at their Christmas show in London, and helped the young Small Faces by introducing them at several venues.
Her self-penned song ‘Just An Excuse’ has been remixed several times, most notably on Bonobo's 2017 album Migration.
Her 1981 album Pearls spent 79 weeks on the UK chart and reached number two, the biggest commercial success of her career.
As a child she sang at bar mitzvahs and weddings; she dates her unofficial debut to a gig at the Laronde club in Manchester, aged 13.

0ZHYWjY4CjSi7BHBiuw3QN.name: 10 Good Songs
f: Ten Good Songs is the independent record label Theo Katzman founded for his own recordings and productions.
In 2023 the label released May Erlewine's album The Real Thing alongside Theo Katzman's Be the Wheel.
The label released Theo Katzman's January 2020 album Modern Johnny Sings: Songs in the Age of Vibe.
In 2025 the label put out Theo Katzman's single ‘Rome Wasn't Built in a Day’.

3l2fkH1yrsHsfYYU2ZnwtI.name: Zohra
f: An Algerian singer born near Constantine in 1950, she was raised on a parental diet of traditional Arabic music.
She took up singing and playing the guitar early, and kept at it after she and her family moved to the north of France.
In her first years in France, she played gala events and receptions.

3A7OTJpEsOObdTqn1ANNhi.name: The Philharmonik
f: Christian Gates, known as The Philharmonik, won NPR's 2024 Tiny Desk Contest with ‘What's It All Mean?’, beating 7,000 other entries.
He explains his stage name by saying he considers himself ‘like a one-man orchestra’.
At his Tiny Desk concert, he kept up the office act of his winning entry, playing the team's boss from a swivelling office chair.
As a child, he came home from a concert with his mother and played the songs he had heard note for note on the piano.
He studied piano ‘by force’ from six to 12; when his family could no longer afford lessons, he learned violin in his middle school orchestra.

3nyoodEXBH2JZUcZuT4KhU.name: Issy Wood
f: Mark Ronson came to her house around New Year, ate most of her blueberries and offered her a deal with his label, Zelig.
Her 2025 portrait of Charli XCX, Charli 2, was commissioned to accompany Vanity Fair's November cover shoot, for its first art-themed issue in 20 years.
She reckons she made at least 70% of her paintings to Matt and Shane's Secret Podcast, and ruined maybe 5% of those laughing so hard her brush slipped.
As a teenager she played bass in a couple of grunge bands, though she quietly yearned to be the frontwoman.
She plays few live shows because she doesn't want to stop painting for long; her concert at Ballroom Marfa was only her fifth.

4WsiLOvvpCEdV40Wg1kzui.name: Zuta
f: Zuzanna ‘Zuta’ Lipowicz said she founded her Poznań duo with Maks Mikulski because she didn't believe she was capable of creating new music.
Getting into the My Name is Poznań project led straight to a Next Fest concert that, Zuzanna ‘Zuta’ Lipowicz said, “changed everything” for the duo.
Their debut EP, Wszystko ja. Wszystko my., pairs a modern approach to making music with a return to 1980s and 1990s dance electronica.

1W4EhwuudqEukgko2blNVo.name: Johnny Parry Chamber Orchestra
f: For Fields & Birds & Things (2012), Johnny Parry stopped working alone and began fronting a 30-piece band, the Johnny Parry Chamber Orchestra.
At Union Chapel in 2012 the orchestra included a saxophone quartet, brass, strings, a choir, a drummer, a bassist, a guitarist and percussionists.
The orchestra performs live in front of films made by Johnny Parry and the artist Andy Holden.

2J4NQiYiPyeo4sTDTeORP8.name: Chen Lo
f: He toured with Jazz at Lincoln Center's Rhythm Road programme, giving workshops and master classes in countries including Morocco, Tunisia, Syria and Honduras.
He starred in five MTV commercials advertising its ‘Sucker Free Week’.
He and Asante Amin make up the music and multimedia duo Soul Science Lab.
He is an adjunct professor at the Roc Nation School of Music at Long Island University.

3NTbCfTrDL2WFob27hdLTe.name: Diane Coffee
f: Diane Coffee is the solo project of Shaun Fleming, an actor who played the twins Jim and Tim Possible in the first three seasons of Kim Possible.
Shaun Fleming says Diane Coffee is not a Twin Peaks reference; he links it to ‘Mr. Coffee’, a song by a singer-songwriter ‘named Nathan Pelkey who never was’.
Shaun Fleming made the project's first album, My Friend Fish, in just under two weeks, recording a makeshift drum kit with his iPhone's voice memo app.
Shaun Fleming never really considered himself a drummer, and only started playing seriously on Foxygen's first tour.
In 2008 Shaun Fleming played Jimmy Livingston in Bubble Boy: The Musical.

3uKe1tF6HSEHFFKfHgpGnj.name: Felicia Douglass
f: She sang lead on Flight Tower, the second of five EPs Dirty Projectors released in 2020, each featuring a different member on vocals.
She didn't play percussion before joining Dirty Projectors, and at first didn't think she could do it.
She has played keyboards and sung in the band Ava Luna since 2008.
By 2015 she had started Gemma, a side project with the producer Erik Gundel.

5nV9SfltxnKK6wselBQAea.name: Michael Farneti
f: He played a kazoo on ‘New York Mugger’ because he couldn't play the saxophone, and multitracked his violin about six times to pass it off as a string section.
He turned down a job offer from a Christian music company; he wanted to get back to Florida and go windsurfing.
He once lived in a tent at the top of a mountain in Costa Rica for about six months.
He bought a two-track Ampex recorder with money earned playing Palm Beach parties as a one-man band, and split a rented space with his father's ad agency.
After Good Morning Kisses he made another album in the 1980s, Looking for a Goddess, but the cassettes he shopped around Nashville came to nothing.

1GqWR6G16qx5tAcRBy5tcw.name: Julia-Sophie
f: As founder of the band Little Fish, she was signed to Universal Motown/Island and toured the USA with Blondie, Courtney Love and Juliette Lewis.
Her band Candy Says co-wrote the score for the indie film Burn Burn Burn and covered ‘Running Up That Hill’ for the Netflix film Close.
She started recording lo-fi pop in her garage, using an old laptop, wonky microphones and whatever was around to hit for beats.
Reflecting on her career, she said she ‘didn't care enough about being famous’ to survive everything that was being thrown at her.

5T4uBooLQ9nO7aDVXomL4A.name: Ben Seal
f: The Tempo House blog introduced them as ‘a producer, musician, Queer dad and “clog activist”’.
They arranged Eliza Carthy's 2020 album Through That Sound (My Secret Was Made Known), and sang on its one cover, the old standard ‘Mean to Me’.
By 2020 they had spent fifteen years producing music, the last seven working out of the Piggery studio in Fife.
A producer and composer across film and music, they have worked and toured with Kathryn Joseph, Rick Redbeard and Bella Hardy.

1kZSI0J6uwTA1q9toxdGqG.name: Segarini
f: The Grateful Dead once asked him to join the band; he turned them down.
His late-night CHUM-FM show as “the Iceman” ended after six months, thanks to a Motörhead interview meant to last 10 minutes that ran for three hours.
His band Family Tree made one album, Miss Butters (1968), now considered one of the first concept albums and inspired by his kindergarten teacher.
He and Randy Bishop co-wrote and recorded two songs, ‘Dear Jesus God’ and ‘Over Me’, for the 1971 film Vanishing Point.

7u3kngt29dTGffr6SZyJwg.name: Dunno
f: The band got its name when someone asked what it should be called and the inspired response was ‘Er… dunno.’
The band had barely rehearsed a set when Emerald Records signed it on 26 April 1971.
The band formed in Belfast in 1971 from a stable of locally popular groups, among them The Dominoes, The Group, Heart and Soul, Chips and The John Smith Band.
As well as complex harmony covers, the band played lesser-known songs such as Bobby Bloom's ‘Heavy Makes You Happy’, Medicine Head's ‘Pictures in the Sky’ and T. Rex's ‘Jeepster’.

4K65oZRtL5hLhKFQXEy3MK.name: Stew & The Negro Problem
f: Mark Stewart, better known as Stew, occasionally answers to the name Burt Blackarach; his hero is Burt Bacharach.
He has played social functions around Los Angeles as the Cover Problem: the patrons choose the set list, but the band plays the songs however it pleases.
He won the 2008 Tony Award for Best Book for Passing Strange, and Spike Lee filmed its final performances for a feature film shown at Sundance.
His first broadcast exposure came from ‘Gary's Song’, which he wrote and performed in 2004 for an episode of SpongeBob SquarePants that aired the next year.
He formed The Negro Problem as a four-piece in the early 1990s; his 2000 album Guest Host was Entertainment Weekly's Album of the Year.

6pGuw52TrX5SZPdQSxAvgW.name: Vulfmon
f: Jack Stratton first adopted the persona of Vulfmon, an old-school German record producer, to promote a Kickstarter for his band Vulfpeck's first vinyl record.
In 2014 his band Vulfpeck released Sleepify, a silent Spotify album whose royalties paid for an admission-free tour.
He helped develop the Vulf Compressor audio plug-in with Goodhertz Inc.
In early comic-music skits, he played characters called Mushy Krongold, Craigs Stewarts and DJ Bean Ornish.

1VqGiwhaU2Djzx8UYFKr2x.name: Izzy Glaudini
f: She is a member of the Los Angeles band Automatic.
She sings on three tracks of Omni's album Souvenir; PopMatters praised her ‘alternately droll and mellifluous voice’.
On first hearing Omni's album Souvenir, PopMatters' reviewer felt she should keep doing duets with Omni's singer Philip Frobos.

2uGpuH0yo0iKx6rBqfgiA9.name: The Joubert Singers
f: Phyliss McKoy Joubert and the choir re-recorded ‘Stand on the Word’ at Trackfire studios in Newark, New Jersey, at the prompting of the French producer Julien Jabre.
At their re-recording session, Phyliss McKoy Joubert's son played piano, and they ended up recording an entire album.
The master tapes of their 1985 session with Tony Humphries and George Rodriguez are thought to have gone up in smoke in 1989.
They were a gospel choir from the First Baptist Church in Crown Heights, Brooklyn.

6haZIHZVYI79wKvp6FCFML.name: Tom A. Smith
f: He played his first gig at the age of eight, supporting the local psychedelic rockers Detroit Social Club.
He had his own radio show on Spark FM in Sunderland for three years, the same show Jordan North had earlier in his career.
He says he has looked at Fiction Records' website about 100 times just to see his name next to The Cure and Tame Impala.
His fans include Nile Rodgers, Tim Booth and Morrissey.
He says he has over 500 songs written.

53tw6ho42crbwJSvI7HPxy.name: Peter Richard
f: Peter Richard was the alias first adopted in 1979 by the producer and vocalist Walter Beinat.
His ‘Walking in the Neon’ was arranged by the Italian disco pioneer Celso Valli.
His music has been played on 15 NTS Radio episodes, including shows with Jamie xx and with Moxie and Leon Vynehall.
His best-known song, ‘Walking in the Neon’, came out as a maxi-single on the Italian label Good Vibes in 1985.
Dark Entries reissued his ‘Walking in the Neon’ on neon orange vinyl, as it had been when first released in 1985.

5xXSrTidFvVRJmiam2Zh1o.name: GENER8ION
f: The duo are director Romain Gavras and composer-producer Surkin, who explore contemporary issues through an ironic near-future lens.
Their 2015 EP with M.I.A., The New International Sound Part II, had a video shot at China's Shaolin Tagou fighting school, featuring synchronised choreography by 36,000 students.
In their video for ‘Storm’, rapper Yung Lean plays a school bully at a Leeds public school in 2034.
For Art Basel Paris in October 2026, they presented God Hates Space at the Grand Palais, an immersive installation that takes visitors to an independent Idaho in 2034.

11DpUQDuQFFuGU8VXny3K6.name: JW Francis
f: Everywhere he goes, he assembles a live band out of fans, a way to keep costs down and make the night memorable.
He says most of his best songs are words he overheard people say, and calls himself ‘kind of secretly a stand-up comedian’.
In early 2023 he was living as a nomad, having left New York after eight years, and planned to spend the year playing backyard shows.
He has hiked the Appalachian Trail, but the sounds of the city inform his music most.
He ran a music blog in 2014, back ‘when blogs were the way you got big’.

2zIBoIRIexK3AUswQWzc7M.name: Jeannie Piersol
f: When she married in 1962, Grace Slick was her maid of honour.
She duetted with Grace Slick in an early line-up of the Great! Society, then fronted her own Bay Area bands, the Yellow Brick Road and Hair.
Her 1968 debut single, ‘Gladys’, was first sent as a demo to Jefferson Airplane, and has Earth, Wind & Fire founder Maurice White on drums.
She left the music industry in the early 1970s to raise children, though she recorded some songs for Sesame Street.

0yz7Rmzzs6xB5eCAVj33A5.name: Smith
f: Their version of ‘The Weight’ is on the Easy Rider soundtrack because, for contractual reasons, the Band’s own version, heard in the film, was unavailable.
Their singer Gayle McCormick had earlier fronted Steve Cummings and the Klassmen, whose 1967 single ‘Without You’ was a local success in Missouri.
Smith grew out of an earlier band with two of the same members, called the Smiths – not the 1980s band.
They managed a few more minor hits and one more album, Minus-Plus, before breaking up.
After leaving music, their singer Gayle McCormick returned home to St. Ann, Missouri, and never resumed her singing career.

4mLJ3XfOM5FPjSAWdQ2Jk7.name: Dr. Dog
f: Their break came in 2004, when Scott McMicken handed My Morning Jacket’s Jim James a CD of Toothbrush decorated with rainbow sprinkles, which caught his eye.
Every member has a nickname beginning with T: former member Andrew ‘Trial’ Jones, for instance, is a licensed attorney.
Since early 2015 their song ‘Warrior Man’ has been the entrance music of the wrestler Matt Sydal in Ring of Honor.
Scott McMicken recorded sessions for Big Thief’s Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe In You live with eight microphones, at one point tracking 13 songs in a single day.
Toby Leaman works as a stone mason, a job he says is ‘really just to stay sane’.

46MOKAqmDsUILZl3iXyPmw.name: Du Blonde
f: She wrote her third album, Homecoming, on a guitar given to her by the Curb Your Enthusiasm actor Jeff Garlin.
Seeing the V&A’s ‘David Bowie Is’ exhibition made up her mind to reinvent herself as Du Blonde: ‘it was almost like the decision was made for me right there’.
Earlier in her career she was locked out of the mixing sessions for her own album because the label said she was being difficult.
She spent only about seven grand making Homecoming, and had already made the money back.
As Beth Jeans Houghton, she directed and illustrated the animated video for the Red Hot Chili Peppers' ‘Sick Love’ in 2016.

3tiDO34wzfyJdv8elYqKxj.name: KOLARS
f: The band was founded by then-husband-and-wife Rob Kolar and Lauren Brown, who had both been members of the folk group He’s My Brother She’s My Sister.
They played over 400 shows, including SXSW, Treefort Festival, The Great Escape and Cornbury, before breaking up in 2021.
Their sound was described as Desert Disco, Space Blues and Glamabilly; Paste said they blended 70s glam rock, 90s grunge and twangy country.

3qWUrXaaCWw9NohGOAKCbD.name: Victor Jones
f: He was born in Manhattan, raised in Charlotte, North Carolina, and started composing before he was ten, writing orchestral scores for short films.
He says the film composer John Williams once gave him notes on a CD he made as a child.
He cites the Pixies and LCD Soundsystem among his inspirations, combined with a later-found love for punk and dance music.
